fact: Highest point of Lithuania: 294 m above sea level. Aukštojas Hill is the highest point of Lithuania. It is located in the Medininkai Highlands, Migūnai forestry, approximately 24 kilometres (15 mi) southeast of the capital city of Vilnius.

title: Boggy Peak
fact: Highest point of Antigua and Barbuda: 402 m above sea level. Boggy Peak is a mountain located in the southwest of Antigua, a constituent island of the archipelagic country of Antigua and Barbuda.

title: Jabal An-Nabi Shu'ayb
fact: Highest point of Yemen: 3,666 m above sea level. Jabal An-Nabī Shuʿayb, also called Jabal Hadhur, is a mountain in the Harazi subregion of the Sarawat, located in Bani Matar District, Sanaa Governorate, Yemen. It is the highest mountain in the country and the Arabian Peninsula.

title: Kneiff
fact: Highest point of Luxembourg: 560 m above sea level. Kneiff is a hill in the Ardennes, in the commune of Troisvierges, in northern Luxembourg, near the tripoint shared with Belgium and Germany.

title: Qurnat as Sawda'
fact: Highest point of Lebanon. Qurnat as Sawdā is the highest point in Lebanon and the Levant, at 3,088 m (10,131 ft) above sea level. It is the summit of Jabal al Makmel, a mountain range in Bsharri District, North Lebanon.

title: Gibson Desert
fact: The Gibson Desert is a large desert in Western Australia, mainly in an almost pristine state. It is about 155,000 square kilometres (60,000 sq mi) in size, making it the fifth largest desert in Australia, after the Great Victoria, Great Sandy, Tanami and Simpson deserts.

title: Annapurna II
fact: 7,937 m above sea level. Annapurna II is the second-highest mountain of the Annapurna range located in Nepal, and the eastern anchor of the range.

title: Chihuahuan Desert
fact: The Chihuahuan Desert is a desert ecoregion designation covering parts of northern Mexico and the southwestern United States.

title: Chappal Waddi
fact: Highest point of Nigeria. Chappal Waddi is located in Nigeria and, at 2,419 m (7,936 ft), is the country's highest point and the highest in West Africa. This peak, whose original and indigenous name is "Gang Peak" is steeped in enthralling ancient Mambilla mythologies.

title: Khazret Sultan
fact: Highest point of Uzbekistan. Khazret Sultan is a mountain in Uzbekistan, with an elevation of 4,643 metres (15,233 ft). It is considered to be the highest point in this country.

title: Mount Tabwemasana
fact: Highest point of Vanuatu: 1,879 m above sea level. Mount Tabwemasana is the highest peak in Vanuatu, and one of the highest mountains in the Pacific.

title: Thabana Ntlenyana
fact: Highest point of Lesotho: 3,482 m above sea level. Thabana Ntlenyana is the highest mountain in southern Africa. It stands 3,482 metres (11,424 ft) tall within the Maloti Mountains that crest Lesotho.

title: Aralkum Desert
fact: The Aralkum Desert is a desert that has appeared since 1960 on the seabed once occupied by the Aral Sea. It lies to the south and east of what remains of the Eastern Basin Aral Sea in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. It is currently the youngest desert in the world.

title: Judaean Desert
fact: The Judaean Desert or Judean Desert is a desert in the West Bank and Israel that stretches east of the ridge of the Judaean Mountains and in their rain shadow, so east of Jerusalem, and descends to the Dead Sea.

title: Api (mountain)
fact: 7,132 m above sea level. Api, also known as Api Himal, is the highest peak in the Yoka Pahar section of the Gurans Himal, a subrange of the western Himalayas.

title: Yangra
fact: 7,422 m above sea level. Yangra (Ganesh I) is the highest peak of the Ganesh Himal, which is a subrange of the Himalayas. Although not an 8,000 metre peak, and little visited, it enjoys great vertical relief over the nearby valleys.

title: Mousa Ali
fact: Highest point of Djibouti: 2,028 m above sea level. Mousa Ali is a 2,021 metres (6,631 ft) stratovolcano located on the tri-point of Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti. The volcano is the highest point in Djibouti.

title: Phnom Aural
fact: Highest point of Cambodia: 1,813 m above sea level. Phnom Aural, also spelled Phnom Aoral, is the tallest peak in Cambodia. It is 1,813 meters tall (other sources give elevations between 1,771 and 1,667 meters). It is in the eastern part of the Cardamom Mountains.

title: Pico de São Tomé
fact: Highest point of São Tomé and Príncipe. Pico de São Tomé is the highest mountain in São Tomé and Príncipe at 2,024 m (6,640 ft) elevation. It lies just west of the centre of São Tomé Island, in the Parque Natural Obô de São Tomé and in the Lembá District.

title: Eastern Desert
fact: The Eastern Desert (known archaically as Arabia or the Arabian Desert) is the part of the Sahara Desert that is located east of the Nile River.

title: Atafu
fact: Atafu, formerly known as the Duke of York Group, is a group of 52 coral islets within Tokelau in the south Pacific Ocean, 500 kilometres (270 nmi; 310 mi) north of Samoa.

title: Jabal al-Nour
fact: Jabal al-Nour is a mountain near Mecca in the Hejaz region of Saudi Arabia. The mountain houses the grotto or cave of Hira.

title: Brandberg Mountain
fact: Highest point of Namibia: 2,573 m above sea level. The Brandberg is Namibia's highest mountain.

title: Bukit Timah Hill
fact: Highest point of Singapore: 164 m above sea level. Bukit Timah Hill is the highest natural peak in Singapore. It is located in Bukit Panjang rather than its namesake district and its altitude is 164 metres (538 feet) above sea level.

title: Jebel ech Chambi
fact: Highest point of Tunisia: 1,544 m above sea level. Jebel ech Chambi is a mountain peak in Tunisia. At an elevation of 1,544 m (5,066 ft), it is the highest mountain in the country. It stands above the city of Kasserine in western central Tunisia.

title: Morne Diablotins
fact: Highest point of Dominica: 1,447 m above sea level. Morne Diablotins is the highest mountain on the Caribbean island of Dominica, and the island's largest and highest volcano. It is the second highest mountain in the Lesser Antilles.

title: Mount Hombori
fact: Highest point of Mali: 1,153 m above sea level. Mount Hombori (Hombori Tondo) is a mountain in Mali's Mopti Region, near the town of Hombori. At 1,155 meters, it is the highest point in Mali.

title: Mount Nyangani
fact: Highest point of Zimbabwe. Mount Nyangani is the highest mountain in Zimbabwe at 2,592 metres or 8,504 feet. The mountain is located within Nyanga National Park in Nyanga District, about 110 km (68 mi) north-northeast of Mutare.

title: Silisili
fact: Highest point of Samoa: 1,858 m above sea level. Mount Silisili is the highest peak in Samoa and the Samoa Islands chain. It is located in the centre of a mountain chain running the length of Savai'i island. Mount Silisili is ranked 24th by topographic isolation.

title: Danakil Desert
fact: The Danakil Desert (or Afar Desert) is a desert in northeast Ethiopia, southern Eritrea, and northwestern Djibouti. Situated in the Afar Triangle, it stretches across 136,956 square kilometres (52,879 mi2) of arid terrain. It is inhabited by a few Afar, who engage in salt mining.

title: Ténéré
fact: The Ténéré is a desert region in south central Sahara. It comprises a vast plain of sand stretching from northeastern Niger to western Chad, occupying an area of over 400,000 square kilometres (150,000 sq mi).

title: Cheekha Dar
fact: Highest point of Iraq: 3,611 m above sea level. Cheekha Dar, which means Black Tent, is the local Kurdish name for the mountain, located in Kurdistan Region of Iraq, currently thought to be the highest in Iraq.

title: Kao (island)
fact: Highest point of Tonga: 1,030 m above sea level. Kao is an island and stratovolcano in the Haʻapai island group of Tonga. It lies about 6 km (3.7 mi) north of Tofua island and reaches 1,030 m (3,379 ft) above sea level, the highest point in Tonga.

title: Monte Binga
fact: Highest point of Mozambique: 2,436 m above sea level. Monte Binga is the highest mountain in Mozambique and the second-highest in Zimbabwe. It is located in the Chimanimani Mountains, straddling the border of Zimbabwe and Mozambique in the Chimanimani Transfrontier Park in…

title: Mount Agou
fact: Highest point of Togo. Mount Agou is the highest mountain in Togo at 986 metres (3,235 ft). It is situated to the south east of Kpalimé in the Plateaux Region of Togo. The mountain lies close to the border with Ghana; this country can be seen from the summit.

title: Mount Liamuiga
fact: Highest point of Saint Kitts and Nevis. Mount Liamuiga is a 1,156-metre (3,792 ft) stratovolcano which forms the north-western part of the island of Saint Kitts.

title: Pico Duarte
fact: Highest point of Dominican Republic: 3,101 m above sea level. Pico Duarte is the highest peak in the Dominican Republic, on the island of Hispaniola and in all the Caribbean.

title: Haramosh Peak
fact: 7,406 m above sea level. Haramosh Peak, also known as Haramosh or Peak 58, is a Karakoram range mountain located in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.

title: Batu Caves
fact: Batu Caves are a series of limestone caves in Gombak, Selangor, Malaysia. It is located on a 325 m (1,066 ft)–tall mogote, about 13 km (8.1 mi) north of the Malaysian capital of Kuala Lumpur.

title: Błędów Desert
fact: Błędów Desert, is an area of sands and gravels located between Błędów and the villages of Chechło and Klucze in Poland. The area lies mainly on the Silesian Highlands in the Lesser Poland Voivodeship.

title: Nanumea
fact: Nanumea is the northwesternmost atoll in the Polynesian nation of Tuvalu, a group of nine coral atolls and islands spread over about 400 miles (640 km) of the Pacific Ocean just south of the equator and west of the International Date Line.

title: Parinacota (volcano)
fact: 6,348 m above sea level. Parinacota (in Hispanicized spelling), Parina Quta or Parinaquta is a dormant stratovolcano on the border of Bolivia and Chile. Together with Pomerape it forms the Nevados de Payachata volcanic chain.

title: Emba Soira
fact: Highest point of Eritrea: 3,018 m above sea level. Emba Soira is the highest mountain in Eritrea. Rising 3,018 metres (9,902 ft) above sea level, it is part of the Eritrean Highlands, one side of the Great Rift Valley which cuts through Eritrea and joins the Red Sea.

title: Emlembe
fact: Highest point of Eswatini: 1,862 m above sea level. Emlembe is the highest mountain in the African country of Eswatini. It is located in the east uKhahlamba (or Drakensberg) mountain range, on the border with South Africa.

title: Mount Bintumani
fact: Highest point of Sierra Leone. Mount Bintumani is the highest peak in Sierra Leone and the Loma Mountains, at 1,945 metres (6,381 ft). It lies in the Loma Mountains and its lower slopes are covered in rainforests, home to a wide variety of animals.

title: Mount Gimie
fact: Highest point of Saint Lucia: 952 m above sea level. Mount Gimie is the tallest mountain on the island of Saint Lucia. It is located in the Canaries District on the west side of Saint Lucia. The mountain's peak reaches 950 m (3,120 ft).

title: Mount Tenakourou
fact: Highest point of Burkina Faso: 749 m above sea level. Mount Tenakourou is the highest point in Burkina Faso. It is a hill situated on the border of the Cascades Region of Burkina Faso and the Sikasso Region of the country of Mali, not far from the source of the Black Volta.

title: Mount Tomanivi
fact: Highest point of Fiji: 1,324 m above sea level. Mount Tomanivi, previously named Mount Victoria and also known as Tomaniivi, is an extinct volcano located in the northern highlands of Viti Levu. At 1,324 metres (4,344 ft), Mount Tomanivi is the highest mountain in Fiji.

title: Jog Falls
fact: Jog Falls is a series of large, segmented waterfalls on the Sharavati River in Karnataka state of India, created by the river plunging approximately 253 metres (830 ft) and splitting into four distinct cascades (Raja, Rani, Roarer, and Rocket).

title: Seokguram
fact: Seokguram is a hermitage and part of the Bulguksa temple complex in Gyeongju, South Korea. It and Bulguksa are both on the mountain Tohamsan, although the two are separated by distance of around 3 kilometres (1.9 mi).

title: Malubiting
fact: 7,458 m above sea level. Malubiting, also known as Malubiting West, ranks as the second highest peak between the Haramosh and Hispar valleys in the Karakoram range in Pakistan. It is situated between Bilchar Dobani and Haramosh Peak, in the Gilgit-Baltistan region.

title: Julianatop
fact: Highest point of Suriname. Julianatop is the highest mountain in Suriname at 1,280 metres (4,199 ft). It is located in the Sipaliwini District. The mountain is named after Juliana of the Netherlands. The Amerindian name of the mountain is Ipinumin (He who stands alone).

title: Monte Pissis
fact: 6,795 m above sea level. Monte Pissis is an extinct volcano on the border of the La Rioja and Catamarca provinces in Argentina, 25 km (16 mi) to the east of the Chilean border and about 550 km (340 mi) north of Aconcagua.

title: Betpak-Dala
fact: Betpak-Dala or Betpaqdala is a desert zone in the Ulytau, Karaganda, Turkestan, and Zhambyl regions, Kazakhstan.

title: Nukunonu
fact: Nukunonu, formerly known as Duke of Clarence Island, is the largest atoll within Tokelau, a dependency of New Zealand in the south Pacific Ocean.

title: Tanami Desert
fact: The Tanami Desert (Warlpiri: Jarnami) is a desert in northern Australia, situated in the Northern Territory and Western Australia. It has a rocky terrain and small hills.

title: Shispare
fact: 7,619 m above sea level. Shispare is one of the high mountain peaks of the Batura Muztagh, the westernmost subrange of the Karakoram range in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan.

title: Teram Kangri
fact: 7,462 m above sea level. The Teram Kangri group is a mountain massif in the remote Siachen Muztagh, a subrange of the Karakoram range.

title: Bukit Pagon
fact: Highest point of Brunei: 1,850 m above sea level. Bukit Pagon (BOO-kit PAH-gon) is the highest point in the country, rising to an elevation of 1,841 metres (6,040 ft) above sea level. It is located in the Temburong District of eastern Brunei, along the border with Sarawak.

title: Cerro El Pital
fact: Highest point of El Salvador: 2,730 m above sea level. Cerro El Pital is a mountain in El Salvador, Central America and near the border with Honduras.

title: Jabal Umm ad Dami
fact: Highest point of Jordan: 1,854 m above sea level. Jabal Umm ad Dami, in historic Wadi Rum, is the highest mountain in Jordan. Its claimed elevation of 1,854 metres is consistent with SRTM data.

title: Kediet ej Jill
fact: Highest point of Mauritania: 915 m above sea level. Kediet ej Jill is a mountain in Tiris Zemmour, Mauritania, with the city of Zouérat on its east and Fderick at west.

title: Mont Ngaoui
fact: Highest point of Central African Republic: 1,410 m above sea level. Mont Ngaoui is the highest mountain in the Central African Republic. It is located on the border with Cameroon and has a summit elevation of 1,410 metres (4,626 ft).

title: Mont Sokbaro
fact: Highest point of Benin. Mont Sokbaro is a mountain that is mostly cited as the highest point of Benin, with an elevation of 658 metres (2,159 ft). This designation is contested, as SRTM readings at coordinates 10°17′22″N 1°32′38″E give an elevation of 672 metres (2,205 ft).

title: Mount Afadja
fact: Highest point of Ghana: 885 m above sea level. Mount Afadja, known as Afadjato to the Ewe people of Ghana and Togo, is one of the highest mountains in Ghana.

title: St. Brandon
fact: Saint Brandon, also known as the Cargados Carajos Shoals, is a southwest Indian Ocean archipelago of sand banks, shoals and islets belonging to the Republic of Mauritius. It lies about 430 km (270 mi) northeast of the island of Mauritius.

title: Goðafoss
fact: Waterfall, 12 m tall. Goðafoss is a waterfall in northern Iceland. It is located along the country's main ring road at the junction with the Sprengisandur highland road, about 45 minutes from Akureyri.

title: Krimml Waterfalls
fact: The Krimml Waterfalls, with a total height of 380 metres (1,247 feet), are the highest waterfall in Austria. The falls are on the Krimmler Ache river and are located near the village of Krimml in the High Tauern National Park in Salzburg state.

title: Nui (atoll)
fact: Nui is an atoll and one of nine districts of the Pacific Ocean state of Tuvalu. It has a land area of 3.37 km2 (1.31 sq mile)and a population of 514 (2022 Census).

title: Nukulaelae
fact: Nukulaelae is an atoll that is part of the nation of Tuvalu, and it has a population of 300 (2017 census). The largest settlement is Pepesala on Fangaua islet with a population of 341 people (2022 Census). It has the form of an oval and consists of at least 15 islets.

title: Reichenbach Falls
fact: Reichenbach Falls is a waterfall in the Bernese Oberland region of Switzerland, which drop a height of 250 metres (820 ft).

title: Darial Gorge
fact: The Darial Gorge is a river gorge on the border between Russia and Georgia. It is at the east base of Mount Kazbek, south of present-day Vladikavkaz. The gorge was carved by the river Terek, and is approximately 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) long.

title: Gangotri Glacier
fact: Gangotri glacier is located in Uttarkashi District, Uttarakhand, India in a region bordering Tibet. This glacier, one of the primary sources of the Ganges, has a volume of over 27 cubic kilometers.

title: Minicoy
fact: Minicoy, locally known as Maliku, is an island in Lakshadweep, India. Along with Viringili, it is on Maliku atoll, the southernmost atoll of Lakshadweep archipelago. Administratively, it is a census town in the Indian union territory of Lakshadweep.

title: Nukufetau
fact: Nukufetau is an atoll that is part of the nation of Tuvalu. The atoll was claimed by the US under the Guano Islands Act some time in the 19th century and was ceded in a treaty of friendship concluded in 1979 and coming into force in 1983.

title: Vaitupu
fact: Vaitupu is the largest atoll of the nation of Tuvalu. It is located at 7.48 degrees south and 178.83 degrees east. There are 1,077 people (2022 Census) living on 5.6 square kilometres (2.2 square miles) with the main village being Asau.

title: Vanch-Yakh Glacier
fact: The Fedchenko Glacier or the Vanch-Yakh Glacier is a large glacier in the Yazgulem Range, Pamir Mountains, of north-central Gorno-Badakhshan province, Tajikistan.

title: Murchison Falls
fact: Murchison Falls, also known as Kabalega Falls, is a waterfall in Uganda, located at the apex of Lake Albert on the White Nile.

title: Scoresby Sound
fact: Scoresby Sound is a large fjord system of the Greenland Sea on the eastern coast of Greenland. It has a tree-like structure, with a main body approximately 110 km (68 mi) long that branches into a system of fjords covering an area of about 38,000 km2 (14,700 sq mi).

title: Tabuaeran
fact: Tabuaeran, also known as Fanning Island, is an atoll that is part of the Line Islands of the central Pacific Ocean and part of the island nation of Kiribati. The land area is 33.73 square kilometres (13.02 square miles), and the population in 2015 was 2,315.

title: Augrabies Falls
fact: The Augrabies Falls is a waterfall on the Orange River, the largest river in South Africa. Since 1966 the waterfall, set in a desolate and rugged milieu, is enclosed by the Augrabies Falls National Park. The falls are around 56 metres (184 ft) in height.

title: Canton Island
fact: Canton Island, previously known as Mary Island, Mary Balcout's Island or Swallow Island, is the largest, northernmost, and as of 2020, the sole inhabited island of the Phoenix Islands, in the Republic of Kiribati.

title: Kegon Falls
fact: Kegon Falls is located at Lake Chūzenji (source of the Oshiri River) in Nikkō National Park near the city of Nikkō, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan. The falls were formed when the Daiya River was rerouted by lava flows.

title: Ouzoud Falls
fact: Ouzoud Falls is the collective name for several waterfalls in the province of Azilal in Morocco. The waterfalls empty into the El-Abid River's gorge.

title: Solway Firth
fact: The Solway Firth is an inlet on the west coast of Great Britain, forming part of the border between England and Scotland. The firth (a Scottish term for an inlet of the sea) divides Cumbria (including the Solway Plain) from Dumfries and Galloway.

title: Tetiʻaroa
fact: Tetiʻaroa is an atoll in the Windward group of the Society Islands of French Polynesia, an overseas territorial collectivity of France in the Pacific Ocean. Administratively, it is part of the commune of Arue.

title: Cascata delle Marmore
fact: The Cascata delle Marmore or Marmore Falls is a tiered, man-made waterfall in Italy, created by the Romans in 271 BC. At 165m (541 feet) tall, it is the largest man-made waterfall in the world. It is located 7.7 km from Terni, in the region of Umbria.

title: Ducie Island
fact: Ducie Island is an uninhabited atoll in the Pitcairn Islands group, which also includes Pitcairn, Henderson and Oeno islands. Ducie lies east of Pitcairn Island, and east of Henderson Island, and has a total area of 1.5 square miles (3.9 km2), which includes the lagoon.

title: Huangguoshu Waterfall
fact: Waterfall, 67 m tall. Huangguoshu Waterfall is the largest waterfall in China and one of the largest waterfalls in East Asia. It is located on the Liuzhi River in Anshun, Guizhou province. It is 77.8 m (255 ft) high and 101 m (331 ft) wide.

title: Jägala Waterfall
fact: Waterfall, 8 m tall. Jägala Waterfall is a waterfall in northern Estonia on the Jägala River. It is the largest natural waterfall in Estonia, with a width of about 50 meters (160 ft) and a height of about 8 meters (26 ft). Jägala Waterfall is located in Koogi in Harju County.

title: Blue Nile Falls
fact: The Blue Nile Falls is a waterfall on the Blue Nile river in South Gondar, Amhara Region, Ethiopia. It is known as Tis Abay in Amharic, meaning 'great smoke'.

title: Breiðafjörður
fact: Breiðafjörður is a large shallow bay of the Irminger Sea, about 50 km (31 mi) wide and 125 km (78 mi) long, to the west of Iceland. It separates the region of the Westfjords (Vestfirðir) from the Snæfellsnes peninsula to the south.

title: Eyjafjörður
fact: Eyjafjörður is one of the longest fjords in Iceland. It is located in the central north of the country. Situated by the fjord is the country's fourth most populous municipality, Akureyri.

title: Hardangerfjord
fact: The Hardangerfjord (English: Hardanger Fjord) is the fifth longest fjord in the world and the second longest fjord in Norway. It is located in the Hardanger region of Vestland county in western Norway.

title: Ironbridge Gorge
fact: The Ironbridge Gorge is a deep gorge, containing the River Severn in Shropshire, England. It was first formed by a glacial overflow from the long drained away Lake Lapworth, at the end of the last ice age.

title: Azykh Cave
fact: Cave: 0.6 km of passages. Azykh Cave, also referred to as Azokh Cave, is a six-cave complex in Azerbaijan, known as a habitation site of prehistoric humans. It is situated near the village of Azykh in the Khojavend District.

title: Glymur
fact: Glymur is a waterfall in Hvalfjarðarsveit, Vesturland, Iceland. It is the second-tallest in the country with a cascade of 198 metres (650 ft). Glymur was long regarded as the tallest until being surpassed by Morsárfoss, a newly measured waterfall near Morsárjökull in 2011.

title: Keila Falls
fact: Keila Falls is a waterfall in northern Estonia on the Keila River. It is the third most powerful waterfall in Estonia after Narva Falls and Jägala Waterfall. It is 6 metres (20 feet) high and 60–70 metres (200–230 feet) wide.

title: Morteratsch Glacier
fact: The Morteratsch Glacier (Romansh: Vadret da Morteratsch) is the largest glacier by area in the Bernina Range of the Bündner Alps in Switzerland. By area and by volume (1.2 km3), it is the third largest glacier in the Eastern Alps, after the Pasterze Glacier and Gepatschferner.

title: Epupa Falls
fact: Epupa Falls is a series of large waterfalls formed by the Cunene River on the border of Angola and Namibia, in the Kaokoland area of the Kunene Region.

title: Guaíra Falls
fact: Waterfall, 40 m tall. The Guairá Falls or Guaíra Falls were a series of immense waterfalls on the Paraná River along the border between Paraguay and Brazil. The falls ceased to exist in 1982 when they were inundated by the impoundment of the Itaipu Dam reservoir.

title: Kalandula Falls
fact: Kalandula Falls or Calandula Falls are waterfalls in the municipality of Calandula, Malanje Province, Angola. On the Lucala River, the falls are 105 meters (344 feet) high and 400 meters (1,300 feet) wide. They are one of the largest waterfalls by volume in Africa.

title: Niah National Park
fact: Niah National Park, located within Miri Division, Sarawak, Malaysia, is the site of the Niah Caves which are an archeological site.

title: Yonaguni Monument
fact: The Yonaguni Monument, also known as the Yonaguni (Island) Submarine Ruins, is a submerged rock formation off the coast of Yonaguni, the southernmost of the Ryukyu Islands, in Japan. It lies approximately 100 kilometres (54 nmi; 62 mi) east of Taiwan.

title: Gocta Cataracts
fact: Gocta is a perennial waterfall with two drops located in Peru's province of Bongara in Amazonas, approximately 771 kilometres (479 mi) to the northeast of Lima. It flows into the Cocahuayco River.

title: Matka Canyon
fact: Matka is a canyon located west of central Skopje, North Macedonia. Covering roughly 5,000 hectares, Matka is one of the most popular outdoor destinations in North Macedonia and is home to several medieval monasteries.

title: Optymistychna Cave
fact: Cave: 265 km of passages, 20 m deep. Optymistychna Cave formerly known as Peshchera Optimistitscheskaya, is a gypsum cave located near the Ukrainian village of Korolivka, Chortkiv Raion, Ternopil Oblast. Approximately 264 km (164 mi) of passageways have been mapped within.

title: Cave of the Apocalypse
fact: The Cave of the Apocalypse is located approximately halfway up the mountain on the Aegean island of Patmos, along the road between the villages of Chóra and Skala. This grotto marks the spot where St. John of Patmos received his visions that he recorded in the Book of Revelation.

title: Columbia Icefield
fact: The Columbia Icefield is the largest ice field in North America's Rocky Mountains. Located within the Canadian Rocky Mountains astride the Continental Divide along the border of British Columbia and Alberta, Canada…

title: Maletsunyane Falls
fact: Waterfall, 192 m tall. Maletsunyane Falls is a 192-metre-high (630 ft) waterfall in the Southern African country Lesotho. It is located near the town of Semonkong (Site of smoke), which is also named after the falls.

title: Manpupuner rock formations
fact: The Manpupuner rock formations are a set of 7 stone pillars located west of the Ural Mountains in the Troitsko-Pechorsky District of the Komi Republic.

title: Pankisi
fact: Pankisi or the Pankisi Gorge is a valley region in Georgia, in the upper reaches of River Alazani. It lies just south of Georgia's historic region of Tusheti between Mt Borbalo and the ruined 17th-century fortress of Bakhtrioni.

title: Ruacana Falls
fact: Ruacana Falls is a waterfall located in Ruacana, Omusati on the Kunene River in Northern Namibia. The waterfall is 120 meters (390 ft) high and 700 meters (2,300 ft) wide in full flood. It is among the largest waterfalls in Africa, both by volume and width.

title: Thwaites Glacier
fact: Thwaites Glacier is an unusually broad and vast Antarctic glacier located east of Mount Murphy, on the Walgreen Coast of Marie Byrd Land.

title: Aldeyjarfoss
fact: Waterfall, 20 m tall. The Aldeyjarfoss waterfall is situated in the Highlands of Iceland at the northern part of the Sprengisandur Highland Road. The river Skjálfandafljót drops here from a height of 20m.

title: Dudhsagar Falls
fact: Dudhsagar Falls is a four-tiered waterfall on the Mahadayi River in the Indian state of Goa. It is 60km from Panaji by road and is located on the Belagavi–Vasco Da Gama rail route about 46km east of Madgaon and 80km south of Belagavi.

title: Kanheri Caves
fact: The Kanheri Caves (Kānherī-guhā ) are a group of caves and rock-cut monuments, cut into a massive basalt outcrop in the forests of the Sanjay Gandhi National Park, on the island of Salsette in the western outskirts of Mumbai, India.

title: Kravica (waterfall)
fact: Kravica Waterfall is a large tufa cascade on the Trebižat River, in the karstic heartland of Herzegovina in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is 10 kilometres (6 mi) south of Ljubuški and 40 kilometres (25 mi) south of Mostar.

title: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
fact: The Southern Patagonian Ice Field, located at the Southern Patagonic Andes between Chile and Argentina, is the world's second largest contiguous extrapolar ice field.

title: Tiger Leaping Gorge
fact: Tiger Leaping Gorge is a scenic canyon on the Jinsha River, a primary tributary of the upper Yangtze River. It is located 60 kilometres (37 mi) north of Lijiang City, Yunnan in southwestern China.

title: Valaste Falls
fact: Valaste Falls is the highest waterfall in Estonia and neighboring regions (30.5 meters or 100 feet).

title: Vinnufossen
fact: Waterfall, 845 m tall. Vinnufossen or Vinnufallet is one of the tallest waterfalls in Europe and the eighth-tallest in the world.

title: Axel Heiberg Glacier
fact: The Axel Heiberg Glacier (85°25′S 163°00′W) in Antarctica is a valley glacier, 30 nautical miles (56 km; 35 mi) long, descending from the high elevations of the Antarctic Plateau into the Ross Ice Shelf (nearly at sea level) between the Herbert Range and Mount Don Pedro…

title: Domica Cave
fact: The Domica cave is a karst cave situated on the south-western border of the Silicka planina Plateau 10 km (6.2 mi) south-east of Plesivec in the Rožňava District of the Košice Region in southern Slovakia.

title: Gutman's Cave
fact: Gutman's Cave is the widest and highest cave in the Baltic countries, located by the Gauja River in the area known as the ancient Gauja valley in the Gauja National Park near Sigulda, Latvia.

title: Kuang Si Falls
fact: The Kuang Si Falls or Kuang Xi Falls, alternatively known as the Tat Kuang Si Waterfalls, is a multi-tiered waterfall in Laos about 29 kilometers (18 mi) south of the town of Luang Prabang. The journey takes 53 minutes from Luang Prabang Night Market downtown.

title: Movile Cave
fact: Movile Cave is a cave near Mangalia, Constanța County, Romania discovered in 1986 by Cristian Lascu during construction work a few kilometers from the Black Sea coast.

title: Vøringsfossen
fact: Waterfall, 184 m tall. Vøringsfossen or Vøringen is the 83rd highest waterfall in Norway on the basis of total fall. It lies at the top of the Måbødalen valley in Eidfjord Municipality in Vestland county.

title: Kebara Cave
fact: Kebara Cave is a limestone cave locality in Wadi Kebara, Israel, situated at 60 to 65 m (197 to 213 ft) above sea level on the western escarpment of the Carmel Range, in the Ramat HaNadiv preserve of Zichron Yaakov.

title: Marble Cave, Kosovo
fact: Cave: 1.3 km of passages. The Marble Cave or the Gadime Cave is a karstic limestone cave in the village of Gadime e Ulët in the municipality of Lipjan in Kosovo. Much of it is still unexplored.

title: Multnomah Falls
fact: Multnomah Falls is a waterfall located on Multnomah Creek in the Columbia River Gorge, east of Troutdale, between Corbett and Dodson, Oregon, United States. The waterfall is accessible from the Historic Columbia River Highway and Interstate 84.

title: Nachi Falls
fact: Nachi Falls in Nachikatsuura, Wakayama Prefecture, Japan, is one of the best-known waterfalls in Japan.

title: Njupeskär
fact: Njupeskär is a waterfall in the river Njupån in Fulufjället National Park, Sweden, about 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) away from the village of Mörkret. With a total height of about 93 metres (305 ft) and a free fall of 70 metres (230 ft), it is the highest free fall in Sweden.

title: Ochtinská Aragonite Cave
fact: Cave: 0.3 km of passages. Ochtinská Aragonite Cave is a unique aragonite cave situated in southern Slovakia, near Rožňava. Although only 300 m long, it is famous for its rare aragonite formations.

title: Sutherland Falls
fact: Waterfall, 581 m tall. Sutherland Falls is a waterfall near Milford Sound in New Zealand's South Island. The falls are located 13.5nm southwest of Chao Pass. At 580 metres (1,904 feet) the falls are among the tallest waterfall in New Zealand.

title: Svartisen
fact: Svartisen is a collective term for two glaciers located in Nordland county in northern Norway. It is part of Saltfjellet-Svartisen National Park, located in the Saltfjell mountain range. The glaciers are located in the municipalities of Beiarn, Meløy, Rana, and Rødøy.

title: Teshik-Tash 1
fact: Teshik-Tash 1 is a Neanderthal skeleton discovered in 1938 in Teshik-Tash Cave, in the Bajsuntau mountain range, Uzbek SSR (Uzbekistan), Central Asia. The remains were discovered in 1938 by A. P. Okladnikov.

title: Torfajökull
fact: Torfajökull is a rhyolitic stratovolcano, with a large caldera (central volcano) capped by a glacier of the same name and associated with a complex of subglacial volcanoes. Torfajökull last erupted in 1477 and consists of the largest area of silicic extrusive rocks in Iceland.

title: Venta Rapid
fact: Venta Rapid is a waterfall on the Venta River in Kuldīga, western Latvia. It is the widest waterfall in Europe at 249 metres (817 ft) across, and becomes as wide as 275 metres (902 ft) during spring floods.

title: Al Naslaa
fact: The Al Naslaa rock (صخرة النصلة) is a landform 50 kilometres (31 mi) south of the Tayma oasis in Saudi Arabia. It is a large sandstone rock split neatly down the middle into two parts, both balanced on small pedestals.

title: Barabar Caves
fact: The Barabar Hill Caves are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, dating from the Maurya Empire (322–185 BCE), some with Ashokan inscriptions, located in the Makhdumpur region of Jehanabad district, Bihar, India, 24 km (15 mi) north of Gaya.

title: Cave of Euripides
fact: The Cave of Euripides is a narrow cave, approximately 47 meters deep with ten small chambers, on a hillside overlooking the Saronic Gulf in the area of Peristeria on the south coast of Salamis Island, Greece.

title: Karla Caves
fact: The Karla Caves, Karli Caves, Karle Caves or Karla Cells, are a complex of ancient Buddhist Indian rock-cut caves at Karli near Lonavala, Maharashtra. It is just 10.9 Kilometers away from Lonavala.

title: Psychro Cave
fact: Psychro Cave is an ancient Minoan sacred cave in the Lasithi plateau in the Lasithi district of eastern Crete. Around the beginning of 20th century, several scholars identified Psychro with Dikte, a name used by some ancient authors to refer to the location of Zeus's upbringing.

title: Cueva de los Verdes
fact: Cueva de los Verdes is a lava tube and tourist attraction of the Haria municipality on the island of Lanzarote in the Canary Islands (Spain). The cave lies within the Monumento Natural del Malpaís de La Corona, a protected area of the Canary Islands.

title: East Antarctic Ice Sheet
fact: The East Antarctic Ice Sheet (EAIS) is the sector of the Antarctic Ice Sheet covering East Antarctica.

title: El Tatio
fact: El Tatio is a geothermal field with many geysers located in the Andes Mountains of northern Chile at 4,320 metres (14,170 ft) above mean sea level. It is the third-largest geyser field in the world and the largest in the Southern Hemisphere.

title: Hogenakkal Falls
fact: Waterfall, 20 m tall. Hogenakkal Falls is a waterfall in South India on the Kaveri river on the border between Dharmapuri district of Tamil Nadu and Chamrajnagar district of Karnataka. It is located 46 km (29 mi) from Dharmapuri and 199 km (124 mi) from Chamrajnagar.

title: Ófærufoss
fact: Ófærufoss is a waterfall situated in the Eldgjá chasm in the western part of Vatnajökull National Park, Iceland. Until the early 1990s a natural bridge spanned the falls, but it collapsed from natural causes.

title: Ramnefjellsfossen
fact: Waterfall, 600 m tall. Ramnefjellsfossen is unofficially listed as the third-highest waterfall in the world in several publications.

title: Smolare Falls
fact: Waterfall, 40 m tall. Smolare Falls is a landform of Macedonia. It is located above the village of Smolare in the Municipality of Novo Selo in the southeastern region of the country.

title: Spannagel Cave
fact: Cave: 10 km of passages. The Spannagel Cave is a show cave near Hintertux, in the Zillertal Alps in the Austrian state of Tyrol. Currently about 10 kilometres of the cave have been discovered; guided tours enable access to 500 metres of the cave.

title: Sphinx (Romania)
fact: The Sphinx is a natural rock formation in the Bucegi Natural Park which is in the Bucegi Mountains of Romania. It is located at an altitude of 2,216 metres (7,270 ft) within the Babele complex of rock formations.

title: Areni-1 cave
fact: The Areni-1 cave complex is an ancient multicomponent site, and late Chalcolithic/Early Bronze Age ritual site and settlement, located near the Areni village in southern Armenia along the Arpa River.

title: Bacho Kiro Cave
fact: Cave: 3.6 km of passages. The Bacho Kiro Cave is situated 5 km (3.1 mi) west of the town Dryanovo, Bulgaria, only 300 m (980 ft) away from the Dryanovo Monastery. It is embedded in the canyons of the Andaka and Dryanovo River.

title: Biafo Glacier
fact: The Biafo Glacier is a glacier located within the Karakoram mountain range in the Hispar Valley, Nagar District of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.

title: Coreca Caves
fact: Coreca Caves are two karstic cavities (Grotta du 'Scuru, cb404, and Gruttuni, cb405) located along the Tyrrhenian coast of Calabria, near Coreca in the municipality of Amantea. The two entrances are very close, about ten yards from each other.

title: Fimbul Ice Shelf
fact: The Fimbul Ice Shelf is an Antarctic ice shelf about 200 km (120 mi) long and 100 km (60 mi) wide, nourished by Jutulstraumen Glacier, bordering the coast of Queen Maud Land from 3°W to 3°E. It was photographed from the air by the Third German Antarctic Expedition (1938–1939)…

title: Folgefonna
fact: Folgefonna is a collective term for three plateau glaciers in the Hardanger region of Vestland county, Norway. They are located on the Folgefonna peninsula in Ullensvang Municipality, Kvinnherad Municipality, and Etne Municipality.

title: Franchthi Cave
fact: Franchthi Cave or Frankhthi Cave is an archaeological site overlooking Kiladha Bay in the Argolic Gulf, opposite the village of Kiladha in southeastern Argolis, Greece.

title: Grand Canyon (Greenland)
fact: The Grand Canyon of Greenland is a tentative canyon of record length discovered underneath the Greenland ice sheet as reported in the journal Science on 30 August 2013 (submitted 29 April 2013), by scientists from the University of Bristol led by Jonathan Bamber…

title: Háifoss
fact: Waterfall, 122 m tall. Háifoss is a waterfall situated near the volcano Hekla in southern Iceland. The waterfall Granni is next to it.

title: Médanos de Coro National Park
fact: Médanos de Coro National Park is a Venezuelan national park located in the state of Falcón, near the city of Coro on the road that leads to Paraguaná. The National Park was created in 1974. The park is easily reached by bus or taxi from Coro.
story_label: Wikipedia: Médanos de Coro National Park

title: Mutarazi Falls
fact: Mutarazi Falls is a waterfall in Mutasa District in Manicaland Province, Zimbabwe. It is located in the 2,495 hectare Mutarazi National Park adjacent to the southern border of the Nyanga National Park.

title: Ngonye Falls
fact: The Ngonye Falls or Sioma Falls is a waterfall on the Zambezi river in Western province Zambia, near the town of Sioma and a few hundred kilometres upstream from the Victoria Falls.

title: Nutty Putty Cave
fact: Nutty Putty Cave was a hydrothermal cave located on state school trust lands, west of Utah Lake in Utah County, Utah, United States, which are managed by the Utah School and Institutional Trust Lands Administration.

title: Ortac
fact: Ortac is a small uninhabited islet about 5 kilometres (3.1 miles) west of the coast of Alderney near to the islet of Burhou. It measures roughly 50 by 70 metres (164.0 by 229.7 feet), and rises 24 metres (78.7 feet) above the sea level.

title: Taylor Glacier
fact: The Taylor Glacier (77°44′S 162°10′E) is a glacier in Antarctica about 35 nautical miles (65 km; 40 mi) long, flowing from the plateau of Victoria Land into the western end of Taylor Valley, north of the Kukri Hills. It flows to the south of the Asgard Range.

title: Three Sisters (Australia)
fact: The Three Sisters are an unusual rock formation in the Blue Mountains of New South Wales, Australia, on the north escarpment of the Jamison Valley.

title: Tottori Sand Dunes
fact: The Tottori Sand Dunes are sand dunes located outside the city center of Tottori in Tottori Prefecture, Japan. With a length of 9 miles (14 km) and a width of less than 1.5 miles (2.4 km), it is the largest sand dune in Japan.

title: Actun Tunichil Muknal
fact: Actun Tunichil Muknal (the Cave of the Crystal Sepulchre), also known locally as ATM, is a cave in Belize, near San Ignacio, Cayo District, notable as a Maya archaeological site that includes skeletons, ceramics, and stoneware.

title: Conventico Caves
fact: The Conventico Caves are a historic cave system in Melilla la Vieja. Accessible through the Museum of Sacred Art in the Spanish city of Melilla, they form part of the Historic Artistic Complex of the City of Melilla, an Asset of Cultural Interest.

title: Ear of Dionysius
fact: The Ear of Dionysius is a limestone cave carved out of the Temenites hill in the city of Syracuse, on the island of Sicily in Italy.

title: Kinderle Cave
fact: Cave: 9.1 km of passages. Kinderle Cave is the second longest cave in the Southern Urals. It is located on the territory of the Zilim Nature Park, 5 km from the village of Tashasti on the right bank of the Kinderle River in Bashkortostan, Russia.

title: Shackleton Glacier
fact: Shackleton Glacier (84°35′S 176°20′W) is a major Antarctic glacier, over 60 nautical miles (110 km; 69 mi) long and from 5 to 10 nautical miles (9.3 to 18.5 km; 5.8 to 11.5 mi) wide…

title: Sumidero Canyon
fact: Sumidero Canyon is a deep natural canyon located just north of the city of Chiapa de Corzo in the state of Chiapas, in southern Mexico.

title: Waimangu Geyser
fact: The Waimangu Geyser, located near Rotorua in New Zealand, was for a time the most powerful geyser in the world. The geyser began erupting in 1900. Its eruptions were observed reaching up to 1,500 feet (460 m) in height, and it excited worldwide interest.

title: Amundsen Glacier
fact: The Amundsen Glacier (85°35′S 159°00′W) is a major Antarctic glacier, about 7 to 11 km (4 to 6 nmi) wide and 150 km (80 nmi) long.

title: Blyde River Canyon
fact: The Blyde River Canyon is a 26 km long canyon located in Mpumalanga, South Africa. It is the third-largest canyon on Earth, behind the Grand Canyon and the Fish River Canyon.

title: Pine Island Glacier
fact: Pine Island Glacier (PIG) is a large ice stream, and the fastest melting glacier in Antarctica. responsible for about 13% of Antarctica's ice loss. The glacier flows west-northwest along the south side of the Hudson Mountains into Pine Island Bay, part of the Amundsen Sea.

title: Upsala Glacier
fact: The Upsala Glacier is a large valley glacier on the eastern side of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Its higher portion lies in a disputed territory between Chile and Argentina.

title: Ferrar Glacier
fact: The Ferrar Glacier (77°46′S 163°00′E) is a glacier in Antarctica. It is about 35 nautical miles (65 km; 40 mi) long, flowing from the plateau of Victoria Land west of the Royal Society Range to New Harbour in McMurdo Sound.

title: Fjaðrárgljúfur
fact: Fjaðrárgljúfur is a canyon in south east Iceland. The Fjaðrá river flows through it. The canyon has steep walls and winding water. It is up to 100 m (330 ft) deep and about 2 kilometres (1.2 miles) long.

title: Boom Gorge
fact: Boom Gorge is a river gorge in Chüy Region and Issyk-Kul Region of Kyrgyzstan. The gorge cuts, in a general north–south direction, across one of Tian Shan's mountain range systems. The range east of the gorge is known as Kyungey Ala-Too, the one to the west is the Kyrgyz Ala-Too.

title: Dniester Canyon
fact: The Dniester Canyon is a canyon formed by the Dniester River, located inside the Dniester River Valley in parts of Ternopil, Ivano-Frankivsk, Chernivtsi, and Khmelnytskyi Oblasts in southwestern Ukraine.

title: Ein Avdat
fact: Ein Avdat or Ein Ovdat is a canyon in the Negev Desert of Israel, south of Kibbutz Sde Boker. Archaeological evidence shows that Ein Avdat was inhabited by Nabateans and Catholic monks.

title: Blue Hole (Red Sea)
fact: The Blue Hole is a diving location on the southeast Sinai, a few kilometres north of Dahab, Egypt on the coast of the Gulf of Aqaba within the Red Sea. The Blue Hole is a blue hole, with a maximum depth within the hole of just over 100 m (330 ft).

title: Columbia River Gorge
fact: Canyon, 1,200 m deep. The Columbia River Gorge is a canyon of the Columbia River in the Pacific Northwest of the United States.

title: Sacred Cenote
fact: The Sacred Cenote is a water-filled sinkhole in limestone at the pre-Columbian Maya archaeological site of Chichen Itza, in the northern Yucatán Peninsula.

title: Arpoador
fact: Arpoador is a region located on the southern zone of the city Rio de Janeiro, in a small peninsula between Ipanema and Copacabana. Part of its territory belongs to the neighbourhood of Ipanema, and part to Copacabana.

title: Garni Gorge
fact: The Garni Gorge is situated 23.3 kilometres (14.5 mi) east of Yerevan, Armenia, just below the village of the same name. The Garni Gorge is protected by law and listed as a natural monument. On a promontory above the gorge, the first-century AD Temple of Garni may be seen.

title: Palo Duro Canyon
fact: Palo Duro Canyon is a canyon system of the Caprock Escarpment located in the Texas Panhandle near the cities of Amarillo and Canyon.

title: Sol de Mañana
fact: Sol de Mañana is an area with geothermal manifestations in southern Bolivia, including fumaroles, hot springs and mud pools. It lies at about 4,900 metres (16,100 ft) elevation, south of Laguna Colorada and east of El Tatio geothermal field.

title: Todgha Gorge
fact: The Todgha Gorges are a series of limestone river canyons, or wadi, in the eastern part of the High Atlas Mountains in Morocco, near the town of Tinghir.

title: Trou de Fer
fact: The Trou de Fer ("Iron Hole") is a canyon on Reunion Island, off the coast of Madagascar in the Indian Ocean. The primary river flowing through the gorge, which is up to 300 m (1,000 ft) deep, is the Bras de Caverne River, a tributary of the Rivière du Mât.

title: Arendsee (lake)
fact: The Lake Arend is a natural lake in the Altmark region, northern Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. It is 23.3 m above sea level, and its area is 5.14 km2, its depth nearly 50 m. It is the largest and deepest natural lake in Saxony-Anhalt.

title: Ásbyrgi
fact: Ásbyrgi is a glacial canyon and forest in the north of Iceland, located approximately 38 kilometres (24 mi) east of Húsavík on the Diamond Circle road.

title: Bimini Road
fact: The Bimini Road, sometimes called the Bimini Wall, is an underwater rock formation near the island of North Bimini in the Bimini chain of islands. The Road consists of a 0.8 km (0.50 mi)-long northeast-southwest linear feature composed of roughly rectangular limestone blocks.

title: Borjomi Gorge
fact: Borjomi Gorge is a picturesque canyon of the Kura River in central Georgia. The gorge was formed as a result of the Kura River cutting its path through the Lesser Caucasus Mountains where the Trialeti and Meskheti Ranges meet.

title: Duinen van Texel National Park
fact: Duinen van Texel National Park (duinen = dunes) is a national park located on the North Holland island of Texel in the Netherlands.
story_label: Wikipedia: Duinen van Texel National Park

title: Ha Gorge
fact: Ha Gorge is a narrow gorge, at the Monasteraki Dakos, on the eastern part of the island of Crete in Greece. It is located in the west slope of Thrypti mountain range, and exits east of Vasiliki village in the plain of Ierapetra.

title: Hierve el Agua
fact: Hierve el Agua is a set of natural travertine rock formations in San Lorenzo Albarradas, Oaxaca, Mexico that resemble cascades of water.

title: Sail Rock
fact: Sail Rock, or Parus Rock, is a natural sandstone monolith of late Cretaceous age located on the shore of the Black Sea, in Krasnodar Krai, Russia. It resembles the outline of a ship's sail, hence its name.

title: Bicaz Gorge
fact: The Bicaz Gorge is a gorge in northeast Romania, in Neamț and Harghita counties. It is in the central part of the Hășmaș Mountains, and is part of the Cheile Bicazului-Hășmaș National Park.

title: Dean's Blue Hole
fact: Dean's Blue Hole is a blue hole located in Long Island, Bahamas in a bay located west of Clarence Town. With a depth of 202 metres (663 ft), it is world's third deepest blue hole after the Taam Ja' Blue Hole in the Chetumal Bay and Dragon Hole in the South China Sea.

title: Deildartunguhver
fact: Deildartunguhver is a hot spring in Reykholtsdalur, Iceland. It is characterized by a very high flow rate for a hot spring (180 liters/second) and water emerges at 97 °C (207 °F). It is the highest-flow hot spring in Europe.

title: Dunajec River Gorge
fact: The Dunajec River Gorge runs through the Pieniny Mountains in the south of Poland and the north of Slovakia (as Dunajec is the border river between the two countries in the area).

title: Laurel Canyon, Los Angeles
fact: Laurel Canyon is a mountainous neighborhood in the Hollywood Hills region of the Santa Monica Mountains, within the Hollywood Hills West district of Los Angeles, California.

title: Steamboat Geyser
fact: Steamboat Geyser, in Yellowstone National Park's Norris Geyser Basin, is the world's tallest active geyser. Steamboat Geyser has two vents, northern and southern, approximately 20 feet (6.1 m) apart.

title: Zwischenahner Meer
fact: is a lake in Ammerland, Lower Saxony, Germany. It is at an elevation of approximately 5 metres (16 ft), and has a surface area of 550 hectares (1,400 acres).

title: Cotahuasi Canyon
fact: Cotahuasi Canyon, near the city of Arequipa in Peru, is one of the deepest canyons in the world.

title: Kings Canyon (Northern Territory)
fact: Kings Canyon, also known as Watarrka, is a canyon in the Northern Territory of Australia located at the western end of the George Gill Range about 321 kilometres (199 mi) southwest of Alice Springs and about 1,316 kilometres (818 mi) south of Darwin…

title: St. Mary's Islands
fact: St. Mary's Islands, also locally known as Thonsepar are a set of four small uninhabited islands in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Malpe in Udupi district of the Indian state of Karnataka.

title: Tsalka Canyon
fact: Tsalka Canyon is part of Khrami (known as Ktsia at its source) gorge near Dashbashi village, 3 km from the small town of Tsalka, in Tsalka Municipality, in Kvemo Kartli region of southeastern Georgia, 1,110-1,448 meters above sea level.

title: Zacatón
fact: Zacatón is a thermal water-filled cenote, or sinkhole, belonging to the Zacatón system – a group of unusual karst features located in Aldama Municipality near the Sierra de Tamaulipas in the northeastern state of Tamaulipas, Mexico.

title: Hveravellir
fact: Hveravellir is a geothermal field (high temperature field) of the Oddnýjarhnjúkur-Langjökull volcanic system - in the north of the Langjökull glacier.

title: Mammoth Hot Springs
fact: Mammoth Hot Springs is a large complex of hot springs on a hill of travertine in Yellowstone National Park adjacent to Fort Yellowstone and the Mammoth Hot Springs Historic District.

title: Bagni San Filippo
fact: Bagni San Filippo is an area in the municipality of Castiglione d'Orcia in the Province of Siena, Italy, not far from Monte Amiata. It is a small hot spring containing calcium carbonate deposits, which form white concretions and waterfalls.

title: Caliphal Baths
fact: The Caliphal Baths are an Islamic bathhouse (or Arab baths) complex in Córdoba, Spain. They are situated in the historic centre which was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1994.

title: Dragon Hole
fact: Dragon Hole, also known as Sansha Yongle Blue Hole after the third Ming emperor, Yongle, was the deepest known blue hole in the world at 300.89 metres (987.2 ft) deep from 2016 until it was discovered that the Taam Ja' surpassed it in 2024.

title: Gunnuhver
fact: Gunnuhver is an active geothermal hot spring and a mud pool with fumaroles on the southwestern tip of the Reykjanes Peninsula in Iceland. It lies within the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark and close to the Reykjanesviti lighthouse.

title: Guanziling Hot Spring
fact: Guanziling Hot Spring is a hot spring in Baihe District, Tainan, Taiwan. The hot spring was discovered by the Japanese troops in the area and it was named Taiwan's No. 1 Hot Spring in 1920. The hot spring is located at an altitude of 270 meters above sea level.

title: Hot Water Beach
fact: Hot Water Beach is a beach on the east coast of the Coromandel Peninsula, New Zealand, just south of Mercury Bay. It is approximately 12 kilometres south east of Whitianga, and approximately 175 kilometres from Auckland by car.

title: Ayn al-Zara
fact: Ayn al-Zara, known in ancient times as Callirrhoe, is an archaeological site in Jordan. It includes the remains of a nymphaeum, though it is considered difficult to be interpreted.

title: Seeburger See
fact: Seeburger See is a lake in the karst region of the Lower Eichsfeld, Landkreis Göttingen, in southeastern Lower Saxony, Germany.

title: Akhayat sinkhole
fact: Akhayat is a sinkhole in Mersin Province, Turkey. The Akhayat Sinkhole is located in a rural area of the Silifke ilçe (district), to the north of Atayurt town.

title: Bimmah Sinkhole
fact: Hawiyyat Najm, known as Bimmah Sinkhole in English, is a water-filled depression, structurally a sinkhole, in the limestone of eastern Muscat Governorate in the Sultanate of Oman, very close to the Al Sharqiyah region just off the highway to Sur, few kilometers before Tiwi.

title: Pozzo del Merro
fact: Pozzo del Merro is a flooded sinkhole in the countryside northeast of Rome, Italy. Situated at the bottom of an 80 m conical pit, at 392 m (1,286 ft) it is the second deepest underwater vertical cave in the world.

title: Taam Ja' Blue Hole
fact: Taam Ja' blue hole is an underwater sinkhole located in Chetumal Bay at the southeast corner of the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico. Its name means deep water in the Mayan language.

title: Aigualluts
fact: The Forau d'Aigualluts is a karst formation and waterfall in the Province of Huesca, northeastern Spain. It lies along the Ésera River, at 2074 m above sea level on Pico Aneto.

title: Bayou Corne sinkhole
fact: The Bayou Corne sinkhole was created from a collapsed underground salt dome cavern operated by Texas Brine Company and owned by Occidental Petroleum.

title: Großes Heiliges Meer
fact: Großes Heiliges Meer is a lake in Hopsten, Kreis Steinfurt, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. At an elevation of 42,5 m, its surface area is 11 ha.

title: Fort Andross
fact: 1632 — The Plymouth Company grants a land patent to Thomas Purchase, the first settler of Pejepscot, Maine, settling at the site of Fort Andross.

title: Turku Cathedral
fact: 1300 — Turku Cathedral is consecrated by Bishop Magnus I in the city of Turku (Swedish: Åbo).

title: Aletschhorn
fact: 1859 — First ascent of Aletschhorn, second summit of the Bernese Alps.

title: Bridgwater
fact: 1685 — Monmouth Rebellion: James Scott, 1st Duke of Monmouth declares himself King of England at Bridgwater.

title: Kiel Canal
fact: 1895 — The Kiel Canal, crossing the base of the Jutland peninsula and the busiest artificial waterway in the world, is officially opened.

title: Banff National Park
fact: 1887 — The Rocky Mountains Park Act becomes law in Canada, creating the nation's first national park, Banff National Park.

title: International Olympic Committee
fact: 1894 — The International Olympic Committee is founded at the Sorbonne in Paris, at the initiative of Baron Pierre de Coubertin.

title: Newfoundland (island)
fact: 1497 — John Cabot lands in North America at Newfoundland leading the first European exploration of the region since the Vikings.

title: Pribilof Islands
fact: 1786 — Gavriil Pribylov discovers St. George Island of the Pribilof Islands in the Bering Sea.

title: Padma Bridge
fact: 2022 — The prime minister of Bangladesh, Sheikh Hasina inaugurates the longest bridge of Bangladesh, Padma Bridge.

title: Illinois Monument
fact: 1914 — The Illinois Monument is dedicated at Cheatham Hill in what is now the Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park.

title: Nakhla meteorite
fact: 1911 — The Nakhla meteorite, the first one to suggest signs of aqueous processes on Mars, falls to Earth, landing in Egypt.

title: Villa Park
fact: 1948 — Boxer Dick Turpin beats Vince Hawkins at Villa Park in Birmingham to become the first black British boxing champion in the modern era.

title: Yosemite Valley
fact: 1864 — U.S. President Abraham Lincoln grants Yosemite Valley to California for "public use, resort and recreation".

title: Battle of Göllheim
fact: 1298 — Battle of Göllheim: Albert I of Habsburg defeats Adolf of Nassau-Weilburg.

title: Pitcairn Island
fact: 1767 — Pitcairn Island is discovered by Midshipman Robert Pitcairn on an expeditionary voyage commanded by Philip Carteret.

title: Sucidava
fact: 328 CE — The official opening of Constantine's Bridge built over the Danube between Sucidava (Corabia, Romania) and Oescus (Gigen, Bulgaria) by the Roman architect Theophilus Patricius.

title: Kolozsmonostor Abbey
fact: 1438 — A temporary compromise between the rebellious Transylvanian peasants and the noblemen is signed in Kolozsmonostor Abbey.

title: Honshu
fact: 869 CE — The 8.4–9.0 Mw Sanriku earthquake strikes the area around Sendai in northern Honshu, Japan. Inundation from the tsunami extended several kilometers inland.

title: Florence Cathedral
fact: 1334 — The bishop of Florence blesses the first foundation stone for the new campanile (bell tower) of the Florence Cathedral, designed by the artist Giotto di Bondone.

title: Dent Blanche
fact: 1862 — First ascent of Dent Blanche, one of the highest summits in the Alps.

title: SS Great Britain
fact: 1843 — Brunel's steamship the SS Great Britain is launched, becoming the first ocean-going craft with an iron hull and screw propeller, becoming the largest vessel afloat in the world.

title: Pendine Sands
fact: 1925 — Malcolm Campbell becomes the first man to exceed 150 mph (241 km/h) on land. At Pendine Sands in Wales, he drives Sunbeam 350HP built by Sunbeam at a two-way average speed of 150.33 mph (242 km/h).

title: Chios
fact: 1319 — A Knights Hospitaller fleet scores a crushing victory over an Aydinid fleet off Chios.

title: King's College Chapel, Cambridge
fact: 1441 — King Henry VI of England lays the foundation stone of King's College Chapel, Cambridge.

title: Kadriorg Palace
fact: 1718 — At the behest of Tsar Peter the Great, the construction of Kadriorg Palace, dedicated to his wife Catherine, begins in Tallinn.

title: Valentia Island
fact: 1866 — The first permanent transatlantic telegraph cable is successfully completed, stretching from Valentia Island, Ireland, to Heart's Content, Newfoundland.

title: Puijo tower
fact: 1963 — The Puijo observation tower is opened to the general public at Puijo Hill in Kuopio, Finland.

title: Quecreek Mine rescue
fact: 2002 — Nine coal miners trapped in the flooded Quecreek Mine in Somerset County, Pennsylvania, are rescued after 77 hours underground.

title: Guanaja
fact: 1502 — Christopher Columbus lands at Guanaja in the Bay Islands off the coast of Honduras during his fourth voyage.

title: Trinidad
fact: 1498 — On his third voyage to the Western Hemisphere, Christopher Columbus becomes the first European to discover the island of Trinidad.

title: Wilberforce Monument
fact: 1834 — Construction begins on the Wilberforce Monument in Kingston Upon Hull.

title: Great Spokane Fire
fact: 1889 — The Great Fire of Spokane, Washington destroys some 32 blocks of the city, prompting a mass rebuilding project.

title: Peace Bridge
fact: 1927 — The Peace Bridge opens between Fort Erie, Ontario and Buffalo, New York.

title: Uraniborg
fact: 1576 — The cornerstone for Tycho Brahe's Uraniborg observatory is laid on the island of Hven.

title: Rocky Mountains
fact: 1842 — The Webster–Ashburton Treaty is signed, establishing the United States–Canada border east of the Rocky Mountains.

title: Mallorca
fact: 1346 — Jaume Ferrer sets out from Mallorca for the "River of Gold", the Senegal River.

title: Enryaku-ji
fact: 1536 — Buddhist monks from Kyoto, Japan's Enryaku-ji temple set fire to 21 Nichiren temples throughout Kyoto in what will be known as the Tenbun Hokke Disturbance.

title: Bayreuth Festival
fact: 1876 — A performance of Wagner's Das Rheingold opens the first Ring cycle at the first Bayreuth Festival.

title: Saint-Domingue
fact: 1791 — Slaves from plantations in Saint-Domingue hold a Vodou ceremony led by houngan Dutty Boukman at Bois Caïman, marking the start of the Haitian Revolution.

title: Wave Hill walk-off
fact: 1975 — Australian Prime Minister Gough Whitlam symbolically hands over land to the Gurindji people after the eight-year Wave Hill walk-off, a landmark event in the history of Indigenous land rights in Australia, commemorated in a 1991 song by Paul Kelly and an annual celebration.

title: Pike Place Market
fact: 1907 — Pike Place Market, one of the oldest continuously operated public farmers' markets in the U.S. and a popular tourist attraction, opens in Seattle, Washington.

title: Sack of Shamakhi
fact: 1721 — The city of Shamakhi in Safavid Shirvan is sacked.

title: Thousand Islands Bridge
fact: 1938 — The Thousand Islands Bridge, connecting New York, United States, with Ontario, Canada, over the Saint Lawrence River, is dedicated by U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt.

title: Tambov Rebellion
fact: 1920 — The Tambov Rebellion breaks out, in response to the Bolshevik policy of Prodrazvyorstka.

title: Possession Island (Queensland)
fact: 1770 — James Cook names and lands on Possession Island, and claims the east coast of Australia for Britain as New South Wales.

title: Nat Turner's Rebellion
fact: 1831 — Nat Turner's rebellion of enslaved Virginians is suppressed.

title: Angoulême Cathedral
fact: 1200 — King John of England, signer of the first Magna Carta, marries Isabella of Angoulême in Angoulême Cathedral.

title: 1883 eruption of Krakatoa
fact: 1883 — The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa begins its final, paroxysmal, stage.

title: Calder Hall nuclear power station
fact: 1956 — The nuclear power station at Calder Hall in the United Kingdom was connected to the national power grid becoming the world's first commercial nuclear power station to generate electricity on an industrial scale.
story_label: Wikipedia: Calder Hall nuclear power station

title: Atauro
fact: 1975 — The Governor of Portuguese Timor abandons its capital, Dili, and flees to Atauro Island, leaving control to a rebel group.

title: Peace Palace
fact: 1913 — Queen Wilhelmina opens the Peace Palace in The Hague.

title: Mainz Cathedral
fact: 1009 — Mainz Cathedral suffers extensive damage from a fire, which destroys the building on the day of its inauguration.

title: Stirling Castle
fact: 1594 — King James VI of Scotland holds a masque at the baptism of Prince Henry at Stirling Castle.

title: Lund Cathedral
fact: 1145 — The main altar of Lund Cathedral, at the time the seat of the archiepiscopal see of all the Nordic countries, is consecrated.

title: Fort Robinson
fact: 1877 — American Indian Wars: Oglala Sioux chief Crazy Horse is bayoneted by a United States soldier after resisting confinement in a guardhouse at Fort Robinson in Nebraska.

title: Greenham Common Women's Peace Camp
fact: 1981 — The first women arrive at what becomes Greenham Common Women's Peace Camp in the UK.
story_label: Wikipedia: Greenham Common Women's Peace Camp

title: La Gomera
fact: 1492 — Christopher Columbus sails from La Gomera in the Canary Islands, his final port of call before crossing the Atlantic Ocean for the first time.

title: Pro Football Hall of Fame
fact: 1963 — The Pro Football Hall of Fame opens in Canton, Ohio with 17 charter members.
story_label: Wikipedia: Pro Football Hall of Fame

title: Millennium of Russia
fact: 1862 — Millennium of Russia monument is unveiled in Novgorod.

title: Battle of Krbava Field
fact: 1493 — Battle of Krbava Field, a decisive defeat of Croats in Croatian struggle against the invasion by the Ottoman Empire.

title: Milwaukee Mile
fact: 1903 — The first race at the Milwaukee Mile in West Allis, Wisconsin is held. It is the oldest major speedway in the world.

title: Bishop Gore School
fact: 1682 — Bishop Gore School, one of the oldest schools in Wales, is founded.

title: Cannikin
fact: 1971 — The first Greenpeace ship departs from Vancouver to protest against the upcoming Cannikin nuclear weapon test in Alaska.

title: San Pedro Bay (Chile)
fact: 1544 — The expedition of Juan Bautista Pastene makes landfall in San Pedro Bay, southern Chile, claiming the territory for Spain.

title: Kōtoku-in
fact: 1498 — The Nankai tsunami washes away the building housing the Great Buddha at Kōtoku-in; it has been located outside ever since.

title: Nukapu
fact: 1871 — Bishop John Coleridge Patteson, first bishop of Melanesia, is martyred on Nukapu, now in the Solomon Islands.

title: St. Olaf's Church, Tyrvää
fact: 1997 — St. Olaf's Church, a stone church from the 16th century in Tyrvää, Finland, is burnt down by a burglar.

title: Little Rock Central High School
fact: 1957 — Little Rock schools integration crisis: President Dwight D. Eisenhower sends the 101st Airborne Division to Little Rock, Arkansas, and federalizes the Arkansas National Guard, ordering both to support the integration of Little Rock Central High School.
story_label: Wikipedia: Little Rock Central High School

title: Sequoia National Park
fact: 1890 — The United States Congress establishes Sequoia National Park.

title: Luzon
fact: 2006 — Typhoon Xangsane passes over Manila after impacting parts of Southern Luzon and Eastern Visayas, becoming the strongest to affect the Philippine capital in 11 years.

title: Maronite Church
fact: 1736 — The Lebanese Council of 1736 begins, a major turning point in the reform of the Maronite Church. In the following three days, the assembled Maronite and Latin clergy presided by Yusuf ibn Siman as-Simani discuss various reforms and elaborate rules and canons.

title: Vulcan Street Plant
fact: 1882 — Thomas Edison's first commercial hydroelectric power plant, the Vulcan Street Plant, begins operation.

title: Montebello Islands
fact: 1952 — The United Kingdom successfully tests a nuclear weapon in the Montebello Islands, Western Australia, to become the world's third nuclear power.

title: Chalk River Laboratories
fact: 1986 — TASCC, a superconducting cyclotron at the Chalk River Laboratories in Canada, is officially opened.

title: Enrico Fermi Nuclear Generating Station
fact: 1966 — A reactor at the Enrico Fermi Nuclear Generating Station near Detroit suffers a partial meltdown.
story_label: Wikipedia: Enrico Fermi Nuclear Generating Station

title: Qantas Flight 72
fact: 2008 — Qantas Flight 72 experiences an in-flight upset near Exmouth, Western Australia, Australia, injuring 112.

title: Peshtigo fire
fact: 1871 — Slash-and-burn land management, months of drought, and the passage of a strong cold front cause the Peshtigo Fire, the Great Chicago Fire and the Great Michigan Fires to break out.

title: Olkiluoto Nuclear Power Plant
fact: 1979 — The Olkiluoto Nuclear Power Plant began operations in Eurajoki, Satakunta, Finland.

title: Morant Bay rebellion
fact: 1865 — Hundreds of black men and women march in Jamaica, starting the Morant Bay rebellion.

title: Java
fact: 1406 — Chen Yanxiang, the only person from Indonesia known to have visited dynastic Korea, reaches Seoul after having set out from Java four months before.

title: San Salvador Island
fact: 1492 — Christopher Columbus's first expedition makes landfall on San Salvador Island in the Caribbean. (Julian calendar)

title: Tomb of Seti I
fact: 1817 — Italian explorer and archaeologist Giovanni Belzoni, uncovered the Tomb of Seti I in the Valley of the Kings.

title: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
fact: 2002 — The Bibliotheca Alexandrina opens in Egypt, commemorating the ancient library of Alexandria.

title: Presidents North Carolina Gave the Nation
fact: 1948 — Presidents North Carolina Gave the Nation, a monument honoring three presidents of the United States, was dedicated at the North Carolina State Capitol in Raleigh, North Carolina.
story_label: Wikipedia: Presidents North Carolina Gave the Nation

title: Battle of Sark
fact: 1448 — Scotland wins a decisive victory over England at the Battle of Sark, the last pitched battle to be fought between the two kingdoms during the Medieval period.

title: Sheffield F.C.
fact: 1857 — Sheffield F.C., the world's oldest association football club still in operation, is founded in England.

title: Malleco Viaduct
fact: 1890 — Malleco Viaduct in Chile, at the time "the highest railroad bridge in the world", is inaugurated by President José Manuel Balmaceda.

title: Lesbos
fact: 802 CE — Empress Irene is deposed and banished to Lesbos. Conspirators place Nikephoros, the minister of finance, on the Byzantine throne.

title: Guadalcanal campaign
fact: 1942 — World War II: The Koli Point action begins during the Guadalcanal campaign and ends on November 12.

title: 1811 Independence Movement
fact: 1811 — Salvadoran priest José Matías Delgado rings the bells of La Merced church in San Salvador, calling for insurrection and launching the 1811 Independence Movement.

title: Last spike (Canadian Pacific Railway)
fact: 1885 — The completion of Canada's first transcontinental railway is symbolized by the Last Spike ceremony at Craigellachie, British Columbia.

title: Provincetown Harbor
fact: 1620 — The Mayflower Compact is signed in what is now Provincetown Harbor near Cape Cod.

title: Joensuu City Hall
fact: 1914 — The Joensuu City Hall, designed by Eliel Saarinen, was inaugurated in Joensuu, Finland.

title: Lions Gate Bridge
fact: 1938 — The Lions Gate Bridge, connecting Vancouver to the North Shore region, opens to traffic.

title: Battle of Cajamarca
fact: 1532 — Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire: Commanded by Francisco Pizarro, Spanish conquistadors under Hernando de Soto meet Incan Emperor Atahualpa for the first time outside Cajamarca, arranging for a meeting in the city plaza the following day.

title: Siege of Lucknow
fact: 1857 — Second relief of Lucknow: Twenty-four Victoria Crosses are awarded, the most in a single day.

title: Tartu Art Museum
fact: 1940 — The Tartu Art Museum is established in Tartu, Estonia.

title: Iran hostage crisis
fact: 1979 — Iran hostage crisis: Iranian leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini orders the release of 13 female and black American hostages being held at the US Embassy in Tehran.

title: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi
fact: 2004 — The Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi, the largest religious building in Georgia, is consecrated.
story_label: Wikipedia: Holy Trinity Cathedral of Tbilisi

title: Mont Granier
fact: 1248 — An overnight landslide on the north side of Mont Granier, one of the largest historical rockslope failures ever recorded in Europe, destroys five villages.

title: 847 Damascus earthquake
fact: 847 CE — An earthquake hits Syria, causing multiple casualties and damages in Antioch, Damascus and Mosul.

title: Maui
fact: 1778 — In the Hawaiian Islands, Captain James Cook becomes the first European to visit Maui.

title: Notts County F.C.
fact: 1862 — Notts County F.C. is founded in Nottingham, England, making it the oldest professional Association football club in the world.

title: FC Barcelona
fact: 1899 — FC Barcelona is founded by Catalan, Spanish and Englishmen. It later develops into one of Spanish and world football's most iconic and strongest teams.

title: Lick Observatory
fact: 1904 — The Jovian moon Himalia is discovered by Charles Dillon Perrine at California's Lick Observatory.

title: Montreux Casino
fact: 1971 — During a concert by Frank Zappa and The Mothers of Invention at the Montreux Casino, an audience member fires a flare gun into the ceiling, causing a fire that destroys the venue. The incident served as the inspiration for Deep Purple's 1973 song Smoke on the Water.

title: Hispaniola
fact: 1492 — After exploring the island of Cuba (which he had mistaken for Japan) for gold, Christopher Columbus lands on an island he names Hispaniola.

title: Aswan Low Dam
fact: 1902 — The opening of the reservoir of the Aswan Dam in Egypt.

title: San Rafael Lake
fact: 1675 — Antonio de Vea expedition enters San Rafael Lake in western Patagonia.

title: Battle of Alton
fact: 1643 — English Civil War: The Battle of Alton takes place in Hampshire.

title: Sylhet Shahi Eidgah
fact: 1782 — British East India Company: Muharram Rebellion: Hada and Mada Miah lead the first anti-British uprising in the subcontinent against Robert Lindsay and his contingents in Sylhet Shahi Eidgah.

title: Ganges Canal
fact: 1851 — India's first freight train is operated in Roorkee, to transport material for the construction of the Ganges Canal.

title: Santiniketan
fact: 1921 — Opening of Visva-Bharati College, also known as Santiniketan College, now Visva Bharati University, India.

title: Nikolauskirche, Oberndorf
fact: 1818 — The first performance of "Silent Night" takes place in the Nikolauskirche in Oberndorf, Austria.

title: Corral Bay
fact: 1670 — The expedition of John Narborough leaves Corral Bay, having surveyed the coast and lost four hostages to the Spanish.

title: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
fact: 1949 — The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, the central bank of the Philippines, is established.

title: Graniteville, South Carolina
fact: 2005 — A train collision in Graniteville, South Carolina, United States, releases about 60 tons of chlorine gas.

title: Calais
fact: 1785 — Frenchman Jean-Pierre Blanchard and American John Jeffries travel from Dover, England, to Calais, France, in a gas balloon.

title: Trans-en-Provence
fact: 1981 — A local farmer reports a UFO sighting in Trans-en-Provence, France, claimed to be "perhaps the most completely and carefully documented sighting of all time".

title: Antarctic Circle
fact: 1773 — Captain James Cook leads the first expedition to sail south of the Antarctic Circle.

title: Second Triumvirate
fact: 38 BCE — Octavian divorces his wife Scribonia and marries Livia Drusilla, ending the fragile peace between the Second Triumvirate and Sextus Pompey.

title: Teatro Filarmonico
fact: 1749 — The Teatro Filarmonico in Verona is destroyed by fire, as a result of a torch being left behind in the box of a nobleman after a performance. It is rebuilt in 1754.

title: Liechtenstein
fact: 1719 — The Principality of Liechtenstein is created within the Holy Roman Empire.

title: Port Egmont
fact: 1765 — A British naval expedition arrives at and names Port Egmont in the Falkland Islands, founding a settlement there eight days later. (Arrival was 15 January 1765 O.S.)

title: Henry Morgan's Panama expedition
fact: 1671 — Original city of Panama (founded in 1519) is destroyed by a fire when privateer Henry Morgan sacks and sets fire to it. The site of the previously devastated city is still in ruins (see Panama Viejo).

title: Hanthawaddy kingdom
fact: 1287 — King Wareru founds the Hanthawaddy kingdom, and proclaims independence from the Pagan Kingdom.

title: Skirmish at Bender
fact: 1713 — The Kalabalik or Skirmish at Bender results from the Ottoman Sultan Ahmed III's order that his unwelcome guest, King Charles XII of Sweden, be seized.

title: Upper Canada
fact: 1796 — The capital of Upper Canada is moved from Newark to York.

title: French West Indies
fact: 1794 — The French legislature abolishes slavery throughout all territories of the French First Republic. It would be reestablished in the French West Indies in 1802.

title: Pagan Kingdom
fact: 1313 — King Thihathu founds the Pinya Kingdom as the de jure successor state of the Pagan Kingdom.

title: Battle of Mansurah (1250)
fact: 1250 — Seventh Crusade: Crusaders engage Ayyubid forces in the Battle of Al Mansurah.

title: Nombre de Jesús (Patagonia)
fact: 1584 — A naval expedition led by Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa founds Nombre de Jesús, the first of two short-lived Spanish settlements in the Strait of Magellan.

title: Lourdes
fact: 1858 — Bernadette Soubirous's first vision of the Blessed Virgin Mary occurs in Lourdes, France.

title: Christ Church Cathedral, Oxford
fact: 1556 — Having been declared a heretic and laicized by Pope Paul IV on 4 December 1555, Archbishop of Canterbury Thomas Cranmer is publicly defrocked at Christ Church Cathedral.

title: Pavia
fact: 1002 — At an assembly at Pavia of Lombard nobles, Arduin of Ivrea is restored to his domains and crowned King of Italy.

title: MS Mikhail Lermontov
fact: 1986 — The Soviet liner MS Mikhail Lermontov runs aground in the Marlborough Sounds, New Zealand.

title: Kherrata
fact: 2021 — Five thousand people gathered in the town of Kherrata, Bejaia Province to mark the second anniversary of the Hirak protest movement. Demonstrations had been suspended because of the COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria.

title: Evangelistas Islets
fact: 1676 — Sixteen men of Pascual de Iriate's expedition are lost at Evangelistas Islets at the western end of the Strait of Magellan.

title: Piedra Movediza
fact: 1912 — The Piedra Movediza (Moving Stone) of Tandil falls and breaks.

title: Compiègne
fact: 888 CE — Odo, count of Paris, is crowned king of West Francia (France) by Archbishop Walter of Sens at Compiègne.

title: Vicenza
fact: 1585 — The Olympic Theatre, designed by Andrea Palladio, is inaugurated in Vicenza.

title: La Scala
fact: 1868 — Mefistofele, an opera by Arrigo Boito, receives its premiere performance at La Scala.

title: Parliament House, Helsinki
fact: 1931 — The Parliament House of Finland is officially inaugurated in Helsinki, Finland.

title: Kingdom of Ireland
fact: 1702 — Queen Anne, the younger sister of Mary II, becomes Queen regnant of England, Scotland, and Ireland.

title: Sakai incident
fact: 1868 — Sakai incident: Japanese samurai kill 11 French sailors in the port of Sakai, Osaka.

title: Rancho San Francisco
fact: 1842 — The first documented discovery of gold in California occurs at Rancho San Francisco, six years before the California Gold Rush.

title: Rmelan
fact: 2016 — Rojava conflict: At a conference in Rmelan, the Movement for a Democratic Society declares the establishment of the Democratic Federation of Northern Syria.

title: Principality of Wales
fact: 1284 — The Statute of Rhuddlan incorporates the Principality of Wales into England.

title: Opéra de Monte-Carlo
fact: 1925 — Ravel's opera L'enfant et les sortilèges, to a libretto by Colette, is premiered at the Opéra de Monte-Carlo.

title: Port Chalmers
fact: 1848 — The ship John Wickliffe arrives at Port Chalmers carrying the first Scottish settlers for Dunedin, New Zealand. Otago province is founded.

title: Vézelay
