fact: 1146 — Bernard of Clairvaux preaches his famous sermon in a field at Vézelay, urging the necessity of a Second Crusade. Louis VII is present, and joins the Crusade.

title: Bechuanaland Protectorate
fact: 1885 — The United Kingdom establishes the Bechuanaland Protectorate.

title: French Sudan
fact: 1960 — France agrees to grant independence to the Mali Federation, a union of Senegal and French Sudan.

title: Septinsular Republic
fact: 1800 — The Treaty of Constantinople establishes the Septinsular Republic, the first autonomous Greek state since the Fall of the Byzantine Empire. (Under the Old Style calendar then still in use in the Ottoman Empire, the treaty was signed on 21 March.)

title: Royal Academy of History
fact: 1738 — Real Academia de la Historia ("Royal Academy of History") is founded in Madrid.

title: San Miguel, Chile
fact: 1925 — Colo-Colo, the most successful and popular soccer football team in the South American nation of Chile, was founded at the El Llano Stadium in San Miguel, Santiago, by footballer David Arellano and some of his teammates who had also left the Deportes Magallanes club.

title: Hilderston, West Lothian
fact: 1608 — A newly nationalized silver mine in Scotland at Hilderston, West Lothian is re-opened by Bevis Bulmer.

title: Fátima, Portugal
fact: 1917 — Three children report the first apparition of Our Lady of Fátima in Fátima, Portugal.

title: Kozhikode
fact: 1498 — Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama discovers the sea route to India when he arrives at Kozhikode (previously known as Calicut), India.

title: Sack of Damietta (853)
fact: 853 CE — A Byzantine fleet sacks and destroys undefended Damietta in Egypt.

title: Shanhai Pass
fact: 1644 — Ming general Wu Sangui forms an alliance with the invading Manchus and opens the gates of the Great Wall of China at Shanhaiguan pass, letting the Manchus through towards the capital Beijing.

title: Council of Constance
fact: 1416 — The Council of Constance, called by Emperor Sigismund, a supporter of Antipope John XXIII, burns Jerome of Prague following a trial for heresy.

title: North magnetic pole
fact: 1831 — James Clark Ross becomes the first European at the North Magnetic Pole.

title: Roquefort-sur-Soulzon
fact: 1411 — King Charles VI grants a monopoly for the ripening of Roquefort cheese to the people of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon, as they had been doing for centuries.

title: Reims
fact: 1775 — The Coronation of Louis XVI in Reims, the last coronation before the French Revolution.

title: British North America
fact: 1846 — The Oregon Treaty extends the border between the United States and British North America, established by the Treaty of 1818, westward to the Pacific Ocean.

title: Assyrian eclipse
fact: 763 BCE — Assyrians record a solar eclipse that is later used to fix the chronology of Mesopotamian history.

title: HMT Empire Windrush
fact: 1948 — The ship HMT Empire Windrush brought the first group of 802 West Indian immigrants to Tilbury, marking the start of modern immigration to the United Kingdom.

title: Abbeville
fact: 1766 — François-Jean de la Barre, a young French nobleman, is tortured and beheaded before his body is burnt on a pyre along with a copy of Voltaire's Dictionnaire philosophique nailed to his torso for the crime of not saluting a Roman Catholic religious procession in Abbeville,…

title: Patriarchate of Aquileia
fact: 1751 — Pope Benedict XIV suppresses the Patriarchate of Aquileia and establishes from its territory the Archdiocese of Udine and Gorizia.

title: Zheng He
fact: 1405 — Ming admiral Zheng He sets sail to explore the world for the first time.

title: Coutances
fact: 1476 — Giuliano della Rovere is appointed bishop of Coutances.

title: Deheubarth
fact: 927 CE — King Constantine II of Scotland, King Hywel Dda of Deheubarth, Ealdred of Bamburgh and King Owain of the Cumbrians accept the overlordship of King Æthelstan of England, leading to seven years of peace in the north.

title: Catalonia
fact: 1849 — Antonio María Claret y Clará founds the Congregation of the Missionary Sons of the Immaculate Heart of Mary, popularly known as the Claretians in Vic, in the province of Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

title: Dieppe
fact: 1632 — Three hundred colonists bound for New France depart from Dieppe, France.

title: Kennewick Man
fact: 1996 — The remains of a prehistoric man are discovered near Kennewick, Washington. Such remains will be known as the Kennewick Man.

title: Amboise
fact: 1469 — Louis XI of France founds the chivalric order called the Order of Saint Michael in Amboise.

title: Matica slovenská
fact: 1863 — Matica slovenská, Slovakia's public-law cultural and scientific institution focusing on topics around the Slovak nation, is established in Martin.

title: House of Representatives (Japan)
fact: 1991 — Takako Doi, chair of the Social Democratic Party, becomes Japan's first female speaker of the House of Representatives.

title: Great Lakes
fact: 1679 — The brigantine Le Griffon becomes the first ship to sail the upper Great Lakes of North America.

title: South Island
fact: 1993 — Two earthquakes affect New Zealand. A 7.0 Mw shock (intensity VI (Strong)) in the South Island was followed nine hours later by a 6.4 Mw event (intensity VII (Very strong)) in the North Island.

title: San Marino
fact: 301 CE — San Marino, one of the smallest nations in the world and the world's oldest republic still in existence, is founded by Saint Marinus.

title: Melfi
fact: 1089 — The first synod of pope Urban II starts in Melfi, with seventy bishops and twelve abbots in attendance. The synod issues several decrees about church law and deals with the relation with the Greek part of the Church.

title: Glastonbury Tor
fact: 1275 — An earthquake occurs in the south of Great Britain, notably causing multiple fatalities as well as destroying St Michael's Church on Glastonbury Tor.

title: Tammerkoski
fact: 1891 — The first hydropower plant of Finland is commissioned along the Tammerkoski rapids in Tampere, Pirkanmaa.

title: Duke of York's Picture House, Brighton
fact: 1910 — The Duke of York's Picture House opens in Brighton, now the oldest continually operating cinema in Britain.
story_label: Wikipedia: Duke of York's Picture House, Brighton

title: Port of Iloilo
fact: 1855 — The Philippine port of Iloilo is opened to world trade by the Spanish administration.

title: Jeanne Mance
fact: 1645 — Jeanne Mance opens the first lay hospital of North America in Montreal.

title: Burma Railway
fact: 1943 — The Burma Railway (Burma–Thailand Railway) is completed.

title: British West Indies
fact: 1774 — American Revolution: The Continental Association, a nonconsumption and nonimportation agreement against the British Isles and the British West Indies, is adopted by the First Continental Congress.

title: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
fact: 1520 — João Álvares Fagundes discovers the islands of Saint Pierre and Miquelon, bestowing them their original name of "Islands of the 11,000 Virgins".

title: West Florida
fact: 1810 — United States annexes the former Spanish colony of West Florida.

title: Union of South Africa
fact: 1922 — A referendum in Rhodesia rejects the country's annexation to the South African Union.

title: Antinoöpolis
fact: 130 CE — Emperor Hadrian establishes the city of Antinoöpolis on the Nile in honour of his companion Antinous, creating a new Hellenizing foundation in Roman Egypt.

title: Dutch East Indies
fact: 1949 — The Dutch–Indonesian Round Table Conference ends with the Netherlands agreeing to transfer sovereignty of the Dutch East Indies to the United States of Indonesia.

title: M10 motorway (Great Britain)
fact: 1959 — The first section of the M1 motorway, the first inter-urban motorway in the United Kingdom, is opened between the present junctions 5 and 18, along with the M10 motorway and M45 motorway.

title: Fashoda Incident
fact: 1898 — France withdraws its troops from Fashoda (now in Sudan), ending the Fashoda Incident.

title: Teatro di San Carlo
fact: 1737 — The Teatro di San Carlo, the oldest working opera house in Europe, is inaugurated in Naples, Italy.

title: Tréguier
fact: 1499 — The Catholicon, written in 1464 by Jehan Lagadeuc in Tréguier, is published; this is the first Breton dictionary as well as the first French dictionary.

title: Battle of Jemappes
fact: 1792 — Battle of Jemappes in the French Revolutionary Wars.

title: Ensisheim
fact: 1492 — The Ensisheim meteorite, the oldest meteorite with a known date of impact, strikes the Earth in a wheat field outside the village of Ensisheim, Alsace, France.

title: Danish West Indies
fact: 1733 — The start of the 1733 slave insurrection on St. John in what was then the Danish West Indies.

title: Pontcysyllte Aqueduct
fact: 1805 — Official opening of Thomas Telford's Pontcysyllte Aqueduct.

title: Schuyler Mansion
fact: 1780 — Founding Father Alexander Hamilton marries Elizabeth Schuyler Hamilton at the Schuyler Mansion in Albany, New York.

title: Messina
fact: 1167 — Sicilian Chancellor Stephen du Perche moves the royal court to Messina to prevent a rebellion.

title: Aire-sur-l'Adour
fact: 484 CE — Alaric II succeeds his father Euric and becomes king of the Visigoths. He establishes his capital at Aire-sur-l'Adour (Southern Gaul).

title: Gadsden Purchase
fact: 1853 — Gadsden Purchase: The United States buys land from Mexico to facilitate railroad building in the Southwest.

title: 1975 British Mount Everest Southwest Face expedition
fact: 1975 — Southwest Face expedition members become the first persons to reach the summit of Mount Everest by any of its faces, instead of using a ridge route.
story_label: Wikipedia: 1975 British Mount Everest Southwest Face expedition

title: Cardiff Metropolitan Cathedral
fact: 1941 — World War II: The Cardiff Blitz severely damages the cathedral in Cardiff, Wales.

title: Presidio San Agustín del Tucsón
fact: 1775 — The Spanish establish the Presidio San Augustin del Tucson in the town that became Tucson, Arizona.
story_label: Wikipedia: Presidio San Agustín del Tucsón

title: Belzec extermination camp
fact: 1942 — The Holocaust in Ukraine: On the Jewish holiday of Yom Kippur, Nazis send over 1,000 Jews of Pidhaitsi to Bełżec extermination camp.

title: Archdiocese of Utrecht (Catholic)
fact: 1248 — The Dutch city of Ommen receives city rights and fortification rights from Otto III, the Archbishop of Utrecht.

title: Texas A&M University
fact: 1876 — The Agricultural and Mechanical College of Texas (now known as Texas A&M) opens as the first public college in Texas.

title: Mor Bar Sauma Monastery
fact: 1166 — Michael the Syrian, one of the most important Syriac historians, is consecrated as Syriac Orthodox Patriarch at the Mor Bar Sauma Monastery.

title: October 2009 Baghdad bombings
fact: 2009 — The October 2009 Baghdad bombings kill 155 and wound at least 721.

title: Hurricane Creek mine disaster
fact: 1970 — Hurricane Creek mine disaster, near Hyden, Kentucky

title: John Brown & Company
fact: 1906 — Cunard Line's RMS Lusitania is launched from the John Brown Shipyard, Glasgow (Clydebank), Scotland.

title: 1975 Algiers Agreement
fact: 1975 — Algiers Accord: Iran and Iraq announce a settlement of their border dispute.

title: Penydarren Ironworks
fact: 1804 — The first self-propelling steam locomotive makes its outing at the Pen-y-Darren Ironworks in Wales.

title: East Indies
fact: 1500 — The fleet of Pedro Álvares Cabral leaves Lisbon for the Indies. The fleet will discover Brazil which lies within boundaries granted to Portugal in the Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494.

title: 1980 Surinamese coup d'état
fact: 1980 — The government of Suriname is overthrown by a military coup led by Dési Bouterse.

title: Mirza Fatali Akhundov
fact: 1873 — The first Azerbaijani play, The Adventures of the Vizier of the Khan of Lenkaran, prepared by Akhundov, is performed by Hassan-bey Zardabi and dramatist and Najaf-bey Vezirov.

title: 16th Street Baptist Church
fact: The 16th Street Baptist Church is a Baptist church in Birmingham, Alabama, United States. In 1963, the church was bombed by Ku Klux Klan members. The bombing killed four young girls in the midst of the Civil Rights Movement.

title: Alamo Mission
fact: The Alamo is a historic Spanish mission and fortress compound founded in the 18th century by Catholic missionaries in what is now San Antonio, Texas, United States.

title: Alcatraz Island
fact: Alcatraz Island is a small island about 1.25 miles offshore from San Francisco in San Francisco Bay, California, near the Golden Gate strait. The island was developed in the mid-19th century with facilities for a lighthouse, a military fortification, and a military prison.

title: Anne Frank House
fact: The Anne Frank House is a writer's house and biographical museum dedicated to Jewish wartime diarist Anne Frank. The building is located on the Prinsengracht, close to the Westerkerk, in central Amsterdam in the Netherlands.

title: ANZAC Cove
fact: ANZAC Cove is a small cove on the Gallipoli peninsula in Turkey. It became famous as the site of World War I landing of the ANZACs (Australian and New Zealand Army Corps) on 25 April 1915.

title: Appomattox Court House National Historical Park
fact: The Appomattox Court House National Historical Park is the preserved 19th-century village named Appomattox Court House in Appomattox County, Virginia. The village was named for the presence nearby of what is now preserved as the Old Appomattox Court House.
story_label: Wikipedia: Appomattox Court House National Historical Park

title: Auschwitz concentration camp
fact: Auschwitz, also known as Oświęcim, was a complex of over 40 concentration and extermination camps operated by Nazi Germany in occupied Poland (in a portion annexed into Germany in 1939) during World War II and the Holocaust.

title: Babi Yar
fact: Babi Yar or Babyn Yar is a ravine in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv and a site of massacres carried out by Nazi Germany's forces during its campaign against the Soviet Union in World War II.

title: Battle of Blair Mountain
fact: The Battle of Blair Mountain was the largest labor uprising in United States history and is the largest armed uprising since the American Civil War.

title: Battle of Bosworth Field
fact: The Battle of Bosworth or Bosworth Field was the last significant battle of the Wars of the Roses, the civil war between the houses of Lancaster and York that extended across England and Wales in the latter half of the 15th century.

title: Battle of Chosin Reservoir
fact: The Battle of Chosin Reservoir, also known as the Chosin Reservoir Campaign or the Battle of Lake Changjin, was a battle in the Korean War. The name "Chosin" is derived from the Japanese pronunciation "Chōshin", instead of the Korean pronunciation.

title: Battle of Kasserine Pass
fact: The Battle of Kasserine Pass was a series of engagements which took place from 19–24 February 1943 around Kasserine Pass, a 2-mile-wide (3.2 km) gap in the Grand Dorsal chain of the Atlas Mountains in west central Tunisia. It was a part of the Tunisian campaign of World War II.

title: Battle of Rorke's Drift
fact: The Battle of Rorke's Drift, also known as the Defence of Rorke's Drift, was an engagement in the Anglo-Zulu War.

title: Battle of the Bulge Monument
fact: The Battle of the Bulge Monument, formerly known as the Mardasson Memorial, is a monument honoring the memory of American soldiers wounded or killed during World War II's Battle of the Bulge.
story_label: Wikipedia: Battle of the Bulge Monument

title: Bay of Pigs
fact: The Bay of Pigs is an inlet of the Gulf of Cazones, located on the southern coast of Cuba.

title: Bergen-Belsen concentration camp
fact: Bergen-Belsen, or Belsen, was a Nazi concentration camp in what is today Lower Saxony in northern Germany, southwest of the town of Bergen near Celle. Originally established as a prisoner of war camp, in 1943, parts of it became a concentration camp.

title: Berghof (residence)
fact: The Berghof was Adolf Hitler's holiday home in the Obersalzberg of the Bavarian Alps near Berchtesgaden, Bavaria, Germany.

title: Bethel Woods Center for the Arts
fact: The Bethel Woods Center for the Arts is an amphitheatre, performing arts center and museum located at the site of the 1969 Woodstock Music & Art Fair in Bethel, New York.
story_label: Wikipedia: Bethel Woods Center for the Arts

title: Blood River
fact: Blood River, also known as the Ncome River, is situated between Nquthu and Vryheid in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

title: Brattahlíð
fact: Brattahlíð, often anglicised as Brattahlid, was Erik the Red's estate in the Eastern Settlement Viking colony he established in south-western Greenland toward the end of the 10th century. The present settlement of Qassiarsuk is now located on the former estate.

title: Bunker Hill Monument
fact: The Bunker Hill Monument is a war memorial on Breed's Hill in the Charlestown neighborhood of Boston, Massachusetts, United States. It commemorates the Battle of Bunker Hill, a major American Revolutionary War battle that took place there on June 17, 1775.

title: Canadian National Vimy Memorial
fact: The Canadian National Vimy Memorial is a war memorial site in France dedicated to the memory of Canadian Expeditionary Force members killed during the First World War.

title: Cape Coast Castle
fact: Cape Coast Castle is one of about forty "slave castles", or large commercial forts, built on the Gold Coast of West Africa (now Ghana) by European traders. Cape Coast Castle is located in the Central Region of Ghana.

title: Cape Trafalgar
fact: Cape Trafalgar is a headland in the Province of Cádiz in the southwest of Spain. Cape Trafalgar lies on the shore of the Atlantic Ocean, northwest of the Strait of Gibraltar.

title: Cecilienhof
fact: Cecilienhof Palace is a palace in Potsdam, Brandenburg, Germany, built from 1914 to 1917 in the look and layout of an English Tudor manor house.

title: Checkpoint Charlie
fact: Checkpoint Charlie (or "Checkpoint C") was the Western Bloc's name for the best-known Berlin Wall crossing point between East Berlin and West Berlin during the Cold War (1947–1991), becoming a symbol of the Cold War, representing the separation of East and West.

title: Chicxulub crater
fact: The Chicxulub crater is an impact crater buried underneath the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico. The crater is named after the onshore inland community of Chicxulub Pueblo.

title: Choeung Ek
fact: Choeung Ek is a site in Dangkao on the outskirts of Phnom Penh, capital of Cambodia, that was used as a Killing Field between 1977 and 1979 by the Khmer Rouge to perpetrate the Cambodian genocide.

title: Colonial National Historical Park
fact: Colonial National Historical Park is a large national historical park located in the Hampton Roads region of Virginia operated by the National Park Service.

title: Corregidor
fact: Corregidor is an island located at the entrance of Manila Bay in the southwestern part of Luzon in the Philippines, and is considered part of Cavite City in the province of Cavite despite being closer to Maragondon and Bataan.

title: Cowpens National Battlefield
fact: Cowpens National Battlefield is a unit of the National Park Service just east of Chesnee, South Carolina, and near the state line with North Carolina. It preserves a major battlefield of the American Revolutionary War.

title: Củ Chi tunnels
fact: The tunnels of Củ Chi are an immense network of connecting tunnels located in the Củ Chi District of Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon), Vietnam, and are part of a much larger network of tunnels that underlie much of the country.

title: Dachau concentration camp
fact: Dachau was one of the first concentration camps built by Nazi Germany and the longest-running one, opening on 22 March 1933. The camp was initially intended to intern the Nazi Party's political opponents, which consisted of communists, social democrats, and other dissidents.

title: Dealey Plaza
fact: Dealey Plaza, named after George Dealey, is a city park in the West End Historic District of downtown Dallas, Texas. It is sometimes called the "birthplace of Dallas", and was the location of the assassination of John F. Kennedy in 1963.

title: Devil's Island
fact: The penal colony of Cayenne, commonly known as Devil's Island, was a French penal colony that operated for 100 years, from 1852 to 1952, and officially closed in 1953, in the Salvation Islands of French Guiana.

title: Douaumont Ossuary
fact: The Douaumont Ossuary is a memorial containing the skeletal remains of soldiers who died on the battlefield during the Battle of Verdun in World War I. It is located in Douaumont-Vaux, France, within the Verdun battlefield…

title: Edmund Pettus Bridge
fact: The Edmund Pettus Bridge carries U.S. Route 80 Business (US 80 Bus.) across the Alabama River in Selma, Alabama, United States.

title: Ellis Island
fact: Ellis Island is an island in New York Harbor, within the U.S. states of New Jersey and New York. Owned by the U.S. government, Ellis Island was once the busiest immigrant inspection and processing station in the United States.

title: Ford's Theatre
fact: Ford's Theatre is a theater in Washington, D.C., which opened in 1863. In 1865, it was the site of the assassination of Abraham Lincoln by John Wilkes Booth. The theater was later used as a warehouse and government office building.

title: Fort Clatsop
fact: Fort Clatsop was the encampment of the Lewis and Clark Expedition in the Oregon Country near the mouth of the Columbia River during the winter of 1805–1806.

title: Fort Duquesne
fact: Fort Duquesne was a fort established by the French in 1754, at the confluence of the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers. It was later taken over by the British, and later the Americans, and developed as Pittsburgh in Pennsylvania.

title: Fort Laramie National Historic Site
fact: Fort Laramie was a significant 19th-century trading post, diplomatic site, and military installation located at the confluence of the Laramie and the North Platte Rivers. They joined in the upper Platte River Valley in the eastern part of the present-day US state of Wyoming.
story_label: Wikipedia: Fort Laramie National Historic Site

title: Fort McHenry
fact: Fort McHenry is a historical American coastal pentagonal bastion fort on Locust Point, now a neighborhood of Baltimore, Maryland.

title: Fort Michilimackinac
fact: Fort Michilimackinac was an 18th-century French, and later British, fort and trading post at the Straits of Mackinac; it was built on the northern tip of the lower peninsula of the present-day state of Michigan in the United States.

title: Fort Necessity National Battlefield
fact: Fort Necessity National Battlefield is a National Battlefield in Fayette County, Pennsylvania, United States, which preserves the site of the Battle of Fort Necessity.

title: Fort Niagara
fact: Fort Niagara, also known as Old Fort Niagara, is a fortification originally built by New France to protect its interests in North America, specifically control of access between the Niagara River and Lake Ontario, the easternmost of the Great Lakes.

title: Fort Ross, California
fact: Fort Ross is a former Russian establishment on the west coast of North America in what is now Sonoma County, California, United States. It was the first multi-ethnic community north of the Spanish missions in what is now the U.S. state of California.

title: Fort Snelling
fact: Fort Snelling is a former military fortification and National Historic Landmark in the U.S. state of Minnesota on the bluffs overlooking the confluence of the Minnesota and Mississippi Rivers.

title: Fort Sumter
fact: Fort Sumter is an incomplete sea fort at the mouth of Charleston Harbor, South Carolina, where the battle that sparked the American Civil War took place.

title: Fort Ticonderoga
fact: Fort Ticonderoga, formerly Fort Carillon, is a large 18th-century star fort built by the French at a narrows near the south end of Lake Champlain in northern New York.

title: Fort Vancouver
fact: Fort Vancouver was an early 19th-century British fur trading post in the disputed region of Oregon Country in the Pacific Northwest. The factory was the principal settlement of the Hudson's Bay Company (HBC) in what was known as the Columbia Department.

title: Fort William Henry
fact: Fort William Henry was a British fort at the southern end of Lake George, in the province of New York.

title: Fulda Gap
fact: The Fulda Gap, an area between the Hesse-Thuringian border, the former Inner German border, and Frankfurt am Main, contains two corridors of lowlands through which tanks might have driven in a surprise attack by the Soviets and their Warsaw Pact allies to gain crossings of the…

title: Gdańsk Shipyard
fact: The Gdańsk Shipyard is a large Polish shipyard, located in the city of Gdańsk, northern Poland. The yard gained international fame when Polish trade union Solidarity (Solidarność) was founded there in September 1980.

title: Gettysburg Battlefield
fact: The Gettysburg Battlefield is the area of the July 1–3, 1863, military engagements of the Battle of Gettysburg in and around Gettysburg, Pennsylvania.

title: Golden Spike National Historical Park
fact: Golden Spike National Historical Park is a United States National Historical Park located at Promontory Summit, north of the Great Salt Lake in east-central Box Elder County, Utah, United States.
story_label: Wikipedia: Golden Spike National Historical Park

title: Gorée
fact: Île de Gorée is one of the 19 communes d'arrondissement (i.e. districts) of the city of Dakar, Senegal.

title: Guilford Courthouse National Military Park
fact: Guilford Courthouse National Military Park, at 2332 New Garden Road in Greensboro, Guilford County, North Carolina, commemorates the Battle of Guilford Court House, fought on March 15, 1781. This battle opened the campaign that led to American victory in the Revolutionary War.
story_label: Wikipedia: Guilford Courthouse National Military Park

title: Gunfight at the O.K. Corral
fact: The gunfight at the O.K. Corral pitted lawmen against members of a loosely organized group of cattle rustlers and horse thieves called the Cochise County Cowboys on October 26, 1881. While lasting less than a minute, the gunfight has been the subject of many books and films.
story_label: Wikipedia: Gunfight at the O.K. Corral

title: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park
fact: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park, originally Harpers Ferry National Monument, is located at the confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers in and around Harpers Ferry, West Virginia.
story_label: Wikipedia: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park

title: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park
fact: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park is a 480-acre (190 ha) National Park Service unit in the U.S. state of Maryland.
story_label: Wikipedia: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park

title: Hellfire Pass
fact: Hellfire Pass, known locally as Chong Khao Kard and in Japanese as Konyu Cutting, is the name of a railway cutting on the former Burma Railway ("Death Railway") in Thailand, which was built with forced labour during World War II.

title: Helmstedt–Marienborn border crossing
fact: The Helmstedt–Marienborn border crossing, named Grenzübergangsstelle Marienborn (GÜSt) (border crossing Marienborn) by the German Democratic Republic (GDR), was the largest and most important border crossing on the Inner German border during the division of Germany.

title: Hiroshima Peace Memorial
fact: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial, originally the Hiroshima Prefectural Industrial Promotion Hall, and now commonly called the Genbaku Dome, Atomic Bomb Dome or A-Bomb Dome, is part of Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park in Hiroshima, Japan…

title: Historic Jamestown
fact: Historic Jamestowne is the cultural heritage site that was the location of the 1607 James Fort and the later 17th-century town of Jamestown in America.

title: Hitsville U.S.A.
fact: "Hitsville U.S.A." is the nickname given to Motown's first headquarters and recording studio. The house is located at 2648 West Grand Boulevard in Detroit near the New Center area of the city. Motown founder Berry Gordy bought the house in 1959.

title: Hỏa Lò Prison
fact: Hỏa Lò Prison was a prison in Hanoi originally used by the French colonists in Indochina for political prisoners, and later by North Vietnam for U.S. prisoners of war during the Vietnam War. During this later period, it was known to American POWs as the "Hanoi Hilton".

title: Hof, Bavaria
fact: Hof is a town on the banks of the Saale river in the northeastern corner of the Upper Franconia region of the German state of Bavaria. The town lies close to the Czech border and is in the forested Fichtel Mountains and Franconian Forest upland regions.

title: Independence Hall
fact: Independence Hall is a historic civic building in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, where both the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution of the United States were debated and adopted by the Founding Fathers of the United States.

title: Iona
fact: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off the Ross of Mull on the western coast of Scotland. It is mainly known for Iona Abbey, though there are other buildings on the island.

title: Iwo Jima
fact: Iwo Jima is one of the Japanese Volcano Islands, which lie south of the Bonin Islands and together with them make up the Ogasawara Archipelago. Together with the Izu Islands, they make up Japan's Nanpō Islands.

title: Jelling stones
fact: The Jelling stones are massive carved runestones from the 10th century, found at the town of Jelling in Denmark. The older of the two Jelling stones was raised by King Gorm the Old in memory of his wife Thyra.

title: John Frost Bridge
fact: John Frost Bridge is the road bridge over the Lower Rhine at Arnhem, in the Netherlands. The bridge was inaugurated after the end of World War II, and is named after Major-General John Dutton Frost (1912–1993)…

title: Joint Security Area
fact: The Joint Security Area (JSA, often referred to as the Truce Village or Panmunjom) is the only portion of the Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) where North and South Korean forces stand face-to-face.

title: Katyn massacre
fact: The Katyn massacre was a series of mass executions of Poles carried out by the Soviet Union between April and May 1940.

title: Kent State shootings
fact: The Kent State shootings were the killing of four and wounding of nine unarmed college students by the Ohio National Guard on the Kent State University campus in Kent, Ohio, United States.

title: Khe Sanh Combat Base
fact: Khe Sanh Combat Base was a United States Marine Corps outpost south of the Vietnamese Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) in Quang Tri province used during the Vietnam War.

title: Kigali Genocide Memorial
fact: The Kigali Genocide Memorial commemorates the 1994 Rwandan genocide. The remains of over 250,000 people are interred there. There is a visitor centre for students and others wishing to understand the events leading up to the Rwanda genocide against Tutsi in 1994.

title: Kings Mountain National Military Park
fact: Kings Mountain National Military Park is a National Military Park near Blacksburg, South Carolina, along the North Carolina/South Carolina border.
story_label: Wikipedia: Kings Mountain National Military Park

title: Kohima War Cemetery
fact: Kohima War Cemetery is a memorial dedicated to soldiers of the 2nd British Division of the Allied Forces who died in the Second World War at Kohima, the capital of the Indian state of Nagaland in April 1944.

title: Kremlin Wall Necropolis
fact: The Kremlin Wall Necropolis is the former national cemetery of the Soviet Union, located in Red Square in Moscow beside the Kremlin Wall. Burials there began in November 1917, when 240 pro-Bolsheviks who died during the Moscow Bolshevik Uprising were buried in mass graves.

title: L'Anse aux Meadows
fact: L'Anse aux Meadows is an archaeological site, first excavated in the 1960s, of a Norse settlement dating to approximately 1,000 years ago.

title: La Isabela
fact: La Isabela in Puerto Plata Province, Dominican Republic was the first stable Spanish settlement and town in the Americas. It was established in late December 1493 to early January 1494. The site is 42 km west of the city of Puerto Plata, adjacent to the village of El Castillo.

title: Landsberg Prison
fact: Landsberg Prison is a prison in the town of Landsberg am Lech in the southwest of the German state of Bavaria, about 65 kilometres (40 mi) west-southwest of Munich and 35 kilometres (22 mi) south of Augsburg.

title: Latin Bridge
fact: Latin Bridge is an Ottoman-era bridge over the river Miljacka in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail
fact: The Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail is a route across the United States commemorating the Lewis and Clark Expedition of 1804 to 1806. It is part of the National Trails System of the United States.
story_label: Wikipedia: Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail

title: Lindisfarne
fact: Lindisfarne, also known as Holy Island, is a tidal island off the northeast coast of England, which constitutes the civil parish of Holy Island in Northumberland.

title: Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument
fact: Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument preserves the site of the June 25 and 26, 1876, Battle of the Little Bighorn, near Crow Agency, Montana, in the United States.
story_label: Wikipedia: Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument

title: Livadia Palace
fact: Livadia Palace is a former summer retreat of the last Russian tsar, Nicholas II, and his family in Livadiya, Crimea.

title: Ludendorff Bridge
fact: The Ludendorff Bridge, also known as the Bridge at Remagen, was the bridge across the river Rhine in Germany which was captured by United States Army forces in early March 1945 during the Battle of Remagen, in the closing weeks of World War II…

title: Ludlow Massacre
fact: The Ludlow Massacre was a mass killing perpetrated by anti-striker militia during the Colorado Coalfield War.

title: Malbork Castle
fact: The Castle of the Teutonic Order in Malbork, commonly known as Malbork Castle, is a Brick Gothic castle complex located in the town of Malbork, Poland, built in the 13th and significantly expanded in the 14th century.

title: Mamayev Kurgan
fact: Mamayev Kurgan is a hill and memorial complex overlooking the city of Volgograd in Southern Russia. The name in Russian means "tumulus of Mamai". The formation is dominated by a memorial complex commemorating the Battle of Stalingrad (July 1942 to February 1943).

title: Manassas National Battlefield Park
fact: Manassas National Battlefield Park is a unit of the National Park Service located in Prince William County, Virginia, United States, north of Manassas.

title: Menin Gate
fact: The Menin Gate, officially the Menin Gate Memorial to the Missing, is a war memorial in Ypres, Belgium, dedicated to the British and Commonwealth soldiers who were killed in the Ypres Salient of World War I and whose graves are unknown.

title: Midway Atoll
fact: Midway Atoll is a 2.4 sq mi (6.2 km2) atoll in the North Pacific Ocean. Midway Atoll is an insular area of the United States, and is an unorganized and unincorporated territory of the U.S. Midway Atoll consists of three islands.

title: Monmouth Battlefield State Park
fact: Monmouth Battlefield State Park is a 1,818-acre (7.36 km2) New Jersey state park located on the border of Manalapan and Freehold Township, in Monmouth County, New Jersey, United States.

title: Monte Cassino
fact: The Abbey of Monte Cassino (today usually spelled Montecassino) is a Benedictine monastery on a rocky hill about 130 kilometres (80 mi) southeast of Rome, in the Latin Valley.

title: Monticello
fact: Monticello ( MON-tih-CHEL-oh) was the primary residence and plantation of Thomas Jefferson, a Founding Father, author of the Declaration of Independence, and the third president of the United States.

title: Moores Creek National Battlefield
fact: Moores Creek National Battlefield is a battlefield managed by the U.S. National Park Service. The park commemorates the 1776 victory of a thousand patriots over about eight hundred loyalists at Moore's Creek.

title: Mount Vernon
fact: Mount Vernon is the former residence and plantation of George Washington, a Founding Father, commander of the Continental Army in the Revolutionary War, and the first president of the United States, and his wife, Martha.

title: Mount Washington Hotel
fact: The Omni Mount Washington Resort is a historic luxury resort hotel in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, United States, near Mount Washington. It was designed by Charles Alling Gifford.

title: Nagasaki Peace Park
fact: Nagasaki Peace Park is a park located in Nagasaki, Japan, commemorating the atomic bombing of the city on August 9, 1945 during World War II. It is next to the Atomic Bomb Museum and near the Peace Memorial Hall.

title: Omaha Beach
fact: Omaha Beach was one of five Allied beach landing sectors of the amphibious assault component of Operation Overlord during the Second World War. On June 6, 1944, the Allies invaded German-occupied France with the Normandy landings.

title: Oskar Schindler's Enamel Factory
fact: Oskar Schindler's Enamel Factory is a former metal item factory in Kraków. It now hosts two museums: the Museum of Contemporary Art in Kraków, on the former workshops, and a branch of the Historical Museum of the City of Kraków, situated at ul.

title: Palace of Justice, Nuremberg
fact: The Nuremberg Palace of Justice is a building complex in Nuremberg, Bavaria, Germany. It was constructed from 1909 to 1916 and houses the appellate court (Oberlandesgericht), the regional court (Landgericht)…

title: Pearl Harbor National Memorial
fact: Pearl Harbor National Memorial is a unit of the National Park System of the United States on the island of Oahu, Hawaii.

title: Pegasus Bridge
fact: Pegasus Bridge, originally called the Bénouville Bridge after the neighbouring village, is a road crossing over the Caen Canal, between Caen and Ouistreham in Normandy.

title: Peleliu
fact: Peleliu (or Beliliou) is an island in the island nation of Palau. Peleliu, along with two small islands to its northeast, forms one of the sixteen states of Palau.

title: Place de la Bastille
fact: The Place de la Bastille is a square in Paris where the Bastille Prison once stood, until the storming of the Bastille and its subsequent physical destruction between 14 July 1789 and 14 July 1790 during the French Revolution. No vestige of the prison remains.

title: Plains of Abraham
fact: The Plains of Abraham is a historic area within the Battlefields Park in Quebec City, Quebec, Canada. It was established on 17 March 1908.

title: Plymouth Rock
fact: Plymouth Rock is a boulder in Plymouth, Massachusetts, United States, which was claimed to have been at the site where the Mayflower Pilgrims landed to found Plymouth Colony in December 1620.

title: Pompeys Pillar National Monument
fact: Pompeys Pillar National Monument is a rock formation located in south central Montana, United States.

title: Port Arthur, Tasmania
fact: Port Arthur is a town and former convict settlement on the Tasman Peninsula, in Tasmania, Australia. It is located approximately 97 kilometres (60 mi) southeast of the state capital, Hobart.

title: Pullman National Historical Park
fact: Pullman National Historical Park is a historic district located in Chicago, Illinois, which in the 19th century was the first model, planned industrial community in the United States.

title: Robben Island
fact: Robben Island is an island in Table Bay, 6.9 kilometres (4.3 mi) west of the coast of Bloubergstrand, north of Cape Town, South Africa.

title: Runnymede
fact: Runnymede is a water-meadow alongside the River Thames in the English county of Surrey, bordering Berkshire and just over 20 miles (32 km) west of central London.

title: Salem witch trials
fact: The Salem witch trials were a series of hearings and prosecutions of people accused of witchcraft in colonial Massachusetts between February 1692 and May 1693. More than 200 people were accused.

title: Sand Creek massacre
fact: The Sand Creek massacre was a massacre of Cheyenne and Arapaho people by the U.S. Army in the American Indian Wars that occurred on November 29, 1864…

title: Saratoga National Historical Park
fact: Saratoga National Historical Park is a United States National Historical Park located in the Town of Stillwater in eastern New York, 30 miles (48 km) north of Albany. The park preserves the site of the Battles of Saratoga.

title: Scapa Flow
fact: Scapa Flow is a body of water in the Orkney Islands, Scotland, sheltered by the islands of Mainland, Graemsay, Burray, South Ronaldsay and Hoy. Its sheltered waters have played an important role in travel, trade and conflict throughout the centuries.

title: Srebrenica Genocide Memorial
fact: The Srebrenica Genocide Memorial, officially known as the Srebrenica–Potočari Memorial and Cemetery for the Victims of the 1995 Genocide, is the memorial-cemetery complex in Srebrenica set up to honour the victims of the 1995 Srebrenica massacre.

title: Stari Most
fact: The Old Bridge, also known as the Mostar Bridge, is a rebuilt 16th-century Ottoman bridge in the city of Mostar in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: Sun Studio
fact: Sun Studio is a recording studio opened by rock-and-roll pioneer Sam Phillips at 706 Union Avenue in Memphis, Tennessee, on January 3, 1950. It was originally called Memphis Recording Service, sharing the same building with the Sun Records label business.

title: Sutter's Mill
fact: Sutter's Mill was a water-powered sawmill on the bank of the South Fork American River in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada in California. It was named after its owner John Sutter. A worker constructing the mill, James W. Marshall, found gold there in 1848.

title: Sutton Hoo
fact: Sutton Hoo is the site of two Anglo-Saxon cemeteries dating from the 6th to 7th centuries near Woodbridge, Suffolk, England. Archaeologists have excavated the site since the discovery of a previously undisturbed ship burial containing a wealth of artifacts in 1938.

title: Templo Mayor
fact: The Templo Mayor was the main temple of the Mexica people in their capital city of Tenōchtitlan, which is now Mexico City. Its architectural style belongs to the late Postclassic period of Mesoamerica.

title: The Cavern Club
fact: The Cavern Club is a music venue on Mathew Street, Liverpool, England. The Cavern Club opened on 16 January 1957 as a jazz club, later becoming a centre of the rock and roll scene in Liverpool in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

title: Thermopylae
fact: Thermopylae is a narrow pass and modern town in Lamia, Phthiotis, Greece. It derives its name from its hot sulphur springs. In Greek mythology the Hot Gates is one of the entrances to Hades.

title: Thiepval Memorial
fact: The Thiepval Memorial to the Missing of the Somme is a war memorial to 72,337 missing British and South African servicemen who died in the Battles of the Somme of the First World War between 1915 and 1918, with no known grave.

title: Þingvellir
fact: Þingvellir was the site of the Alþing, the annual parliament of Iceland from the year 930 until the last session held at Þingvellir in 1798.

title: Tiananmen Square
fact: Tiananmen Square or Tian'anmen Square is a city square in the city centre of Beijing, China, named after the Tiananmen ("Gate of Heavenly Peace") located to its north, which separates it from the Forbidden City imperial palace complex.

title: Tora Bora
fact: Tora Bora is a cave complex, part of the Spin Ghar (White Mountains) mountain range of eastern Afghanistan.

title: Tower of London
fact: The Tower of London, officially His Majesty's Royal Palace and Fortress of the Tower of London, is a historic citadel and castle on the north bank of the River Thames in London, England.

title: Treblinka extermination camp
fact: Treblinka was the second-deadliest extermination camp to be built and operated by Nazi Germany in occupied Poland during World War II, second only to Auschwitz.

title: Trenton Battle Monument
fact: The Trenton Battle Monument is a massive column-type structure in the Battle Monument section of Trenton, Mercer County, New Jersey, United States.

title: Tunguska event
fact: The Tunguska event was the explosion of between 3 and 50 megatons TNT equivalent in the Russian Empire's Yeniseysk Governorate, near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in modern Krasnoyarsk Krai, on the morning of 30 June 1908.

title: Valley Forge
fact: Valley Forge was the winter encampment of the Continental Army, under the command of George Washington, during the Philadelphia campaign of the American Revolutionary War.

title: Vicksburg National Military Park
fact: Vicksburg National Military Park preserves the site of the Siege of Vicksburg, waged from March 29 to July 4, 1863 during the American Civil War.

title: Vilcabamba, Peru
fact: Vilcabamba (in Hispanicized spelling) or Willkapampa, often called the Lost City of the Incas, is a lost city in the Echarate District of La Convención Province in the Cuzco Region of Peru. Vilcabamba, in Quechua, means "sacred plain".

title: Vukovar water tower
fact: The Vukovar water tower is a structure in Vukovar, Croatia. Built in 1968 in the Socialist Republic of Croatia in Yugoslavia, it became a symbol of the Croatian War of Independence.

title: Warsaw Uprising Monument
fact: Warsaw Uprising Monument is a monument in Warsaw, Poland, dedicated to the Warsaw Uprising of 1944. Unveiled in 1989, it was designed by Jacek Budyn and sculpted by Wincenty Kućma. It is located on the southern side of Krasiński Square.

title: Whitney Plantation Historic District
fact: The Whitney Plantation Historic District is preserved by the Whitney Institute, a non-profit whose mission is to educate the public about the history and legacies of slavery in the Southern United States.

title: Winter Palace
fact: The Winter Palace is a palace in Saint Petersburg that served as the official residence of the House of Romanov, the emperors of Russia, from 1732 to 1917. The palace and its precincts now house the Hermitage Museum. The floor area is 233,345 square metres.

title: Wolf's Lair
fact: The Wolf's Lair was Adolf Hitler's first Eastern Front military headquarters in World War II. Currently, it is a museum open to the public, as well as a hotel, conference room and restaurant.

title: Women's Rights National Historical Park
fact: The Women's Rights National Historical Park is a United States National Historical Park in Seneca Falls and Waterloo, New York, United States. Founded by an act of Congress in 1980, the park was first opened in 1982.
story_label: Wikipedia: Women's Rights National Historical Park

title: Wounded Knee Massacre
fact: The Wounded Knee Massacre, also known as the Battle of Wounded Knee, was an 1890 armed conflict between Native Americans and the United States Army. It was part of the U.S. Army’s Pine Ridge Campaign.

title: Wright Brothers National Memorial
fact: Wright Brothers National Memorial (originally the Kill Devil Hill Monument), located in Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina, commemorates Wright Flyer; the first successful, sustained, powered flights in a heavier-than-air machine.

title: Yad Vashem
fact: Yad Vashem is Israel's official memorial institution to the victims of the Holocaust, known in Hebrew as the Shoah (שואה).

title: 1420 Caldera earthquake
fact: 1420 — The 8.8–9.4 Caldera earthquake shakes Chile's Atacama Region causing tsunami in Chile, Hawaii, and Japan.

title: Battle of the Thames
fact: 1813 — War of 1812: The Army of the Northwest defeats a British and Native Canadian force threatening Detroit.

title: Imilac
fact: Imilac is a pallasite meteorite found in the Atacama Desert of Northern Chile in 1822.

title: Itqiy meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1990. The Itqiy meteorite is an enstatite-rich stony-iron meteorite. It is classified as an enstatite chondrite of the EH group that was nearly melted and is therefore very unusual for that group.

title: Neuschwanstein (meteorite)
fact: Neuschwanstein was an enstatite chondrite (type EL6) meteorite that fell to Earth on 6 April 2002 at 22:20:18 GMT near Neuschwanstein Castle, Bavaria, at the Germany–Austria border.

title: Old Woman meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1975. The Old Woman Meteorite is the largest meteorite to have been found in California and the second largest in the United States. It was discovered in the Old Woman Mountains in southern California in late March 1976.

title: Tenham (meteorite)
fact: Tenham meteorites are the fragments of a larger meteorite that fell in 1879 in a remote area of Australia near the Tenham station, South Gregory, in western Queensland. Although the fall was seen by a number of people, its exact date has not been established.

title: Ames crater
fact: Ames crater is a meteorite crater (astrobleme) in Major County, Oklahoma, United States. Ames, Oklahoma is near the center of the structure, which is 30 miles (48 km) southwest of Enid, Oklahoma. Buried under a thick layer of sediment, it was not discovered until 1991.

title: Bedout
fact: Bedout, or more specifically the Bedout High, is a geological and geophysical feature centered about 250 km (160 miles) off the northwestern coast of Australia in the Canning and overlying Roebuck basins.

title: BP Impact Structure
fact: The BP Impact Structure, also known as Gebel Dalma, is a deeply eroded impact structure that is located 165 km (103 mi) northeast of the Kufra Oasis in southwest Libya.

title: Burckle Crater
fact: The Burckle crater is an undersea topographic feature about 29 kilometres (18 mi; 16 nmi) in diameter in the southwestern Indian Ocean.

title: Chukcha crater
fact: Chukcha is an impact crater in Taimyr Peninsula, Russia. It is 6 kilometres (3.7 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 70 million years old (Cretaceous or younger). The crater is exposed to the surface.

title: Crawford crater
fact: Crawford is an impact crater near Adelaide in South Australia, Australia. The Crawford crater is up to 8.5 km long, and is thought to have been formed by oblique (low angle) impact. Its age is estimated to be greater than 35 million years (probably Eocene).

title: Dalgaranga crater
fact: Dalgaranga crater is a small meteorite impact crater located on Dalgaranga pastoral station 75 km (47 mi) northwest of Mount Magnet (or north of Yalgoo) in Western Australia.

title: Goat Paddock crater
fact: Goat Paddock Crater is an impact crater in a range of gently dipping Proterozoic sandstone in the Kimberley Region of northern Western Australia, 106 km west-southwest of Halls Creek.

title: Goyder crater
fact: Goyder is an impact structure (or astrobleme), the eroded remnant of a former impact crater. It is situated in Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, Australia, and was named after the nearby Goyder River.

title: Haviland Crater
fact: The Haviland Crater, also called the Brenham Crater, is a meteorite crater (astrobleme) in Kiowa County, Kansas. The oval crater is 50 feet (15 m) in diameter, making it one of the smallest impact craters in the world. Its age is estimated to be less than 1,000 years.

title: Kamil Crater
fact: The Kamil Crater is a 44.8-metre-wide (147 ft) and 15.8-metre-deep (52 ft) (original depth, a part covered by sand at present) meteorite impact crater in the East Uweinat Desert in southwestern New Valley Governorate, Egypt…

title: Luizi crater
fact: Luizi is a meteorite impact structure that lies on the Kundelungu Plateau of Haut-Katanga province, in an underexplored region of southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

title: Mahuika crater
fact: Mahuika crater was a hypothesized impact crater named after the Māori god of fire. It was described as being about 20 ± 2 km (12.4 ± 1.2 mi) wide and over 153 meters (502 ft) deep and on the New Zealand continental shelf at 48.3 South and 166.4 East, to the south of The Snares.

title: Nicholson crater
fact: Nicholson is a meteorite crater in the Northwest Territories, Canada. It is 12.5 kilometres (7.8 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 400 million years (Devonian or earlier). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Piccaninny crater
fact: Piccaninny crater is an impact structure, the eroded remnant of a former impact crater, situated in northern Western Australia in the Kimberley region. It was named after Piccaninny Creek and lies within the Purnululu (Bungle Bungle) National Park.

title: Pilot crater
fact: Impact crater, 6 km across. Pilot crater is an impact crater in the Northwest Territories, Canada, just north of the Alberta border and near Fort Smith 54 km (34 mi). It is 6 km (3.7 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 445 ± 2 million years (Upper Ordovician).

title: Ragozinka crater
fact: Ragozinka is a meteorite crater in the Urals in Russia. It is 9 kilometres (5.6 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 46 ± 3 million years old (Eocene). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Riachão Ring
fact: The Riachão Ring is a meteorite impact crater in Brazil. It lies within the Parnaíba Basin. It is 4.5 kilometres (2.8 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be less than 200 million years (Jurassic or younger). The crater is exposed at the surface.

title: Sierra Madera crater
fact: The Sierra Madera crater is a complex impact crater (astrobleme) in southwestern Pecos County, Texas, United States.

title: Vista Alegre crater
fact: The Vista Alegre crater is a meteorite crater in Coronel Vivida, Paraná State, Brazil. On the surface it appears as a circular, relatively flat plain within otherwise hilly terrain.

title: Wells Creek crater
fact: Wells Creek is an impact crater located near Cumberland City, Tennessee. It is 12 kilometers (7.5 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 200±100 Ma (million years old), placing it in the Jurassic or a neighboring period. The crater is exposed to the surface.

title: Zapadnaya crater
fact: Zapadnaya (Bilylivka) is an impact crater in Ukraine near the village of Bilylivka in the southeasternmost edge of Zhytomyr Oblast and near the border of Vinnytsia Oblast. It is situated in the northwestern part of the Ukrainian crystalline shield.

title: Zeleny Gai crater
fact: Zeleny Gai is an impact crater in Ukraine (Kirovohrad Oblast). It is 3.5 kilometres (2.2 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 80 ± 20 million years (Upper Cretaceous). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Akbarpur (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 1.8 kg. Akbarpur is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on April 18, 1838, in Uttar Pradesh, India. It is notable for being the first Indian meteorite for which an official report accompanied by a legal deposition was filed.

title: Allegan (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 32 kg. Allegan is a type 5 H chondrite meteorite that landed west of Allegan, Michigan on July 10, 1899. Allegan weighed around fifty pounds after its landing. As of 1964, it was one of only seven known meteorites to land in Michigan.

title: Avanhandava (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 9.3 kg. Avanhandava is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth in 1952 in São Paulo, Brazil. It is classified as H4-ordinary chondrite. A total of 9.33 kilograms (20.6 lb) of this meteorite was collected after it broke up during its impact with the Earth.

title: Elbogen (meteorite)
fact: Elbogen, also the Loket Iron, is an iron meteorite that fell in the town of Loket, Karlovy Vary Region, Kingdom of Bohemia, about the year 1400.

title: Goose Lake meteorite
fact: The Goose Lake meteorite is a meteorite that was found at Goose Lake in the United States by two hunters from Oakland, California on October 13, 1938. In 1939 it was acquired by the United States National Museum.

title: Karoonda meteorite
fact: The Karoonda meteorite is a meteorite that fell to earth on 25 November 1930 at 10:53 pm near the South Australian town of Karoonda. It is of a rare composition, being carbonaceous chondrite, and is also rare in that it was found so soon after its landing.

title: Kesen meteorite
fact: The Kesen meteorite fell on 13 June 1850, landing in a swamp in the outskirts of the city of Rikuzentakata, Kesen District in Iwate Prefecture, Japan.

title: Park Forest (meteorite)
fact: Park Forest is an L5 chondrite meteorite that fell on 26 March 2003 in Illinois, United States.

title: Patos de Minas (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite, 200 kg. Patos de Minas is an octahedrite meteorite. It was found in 1925 and 2002 in Patos de Minas, Minas Gerais, Brazil. It weighs 200 kilograms (440 lb) and has average dimensions of 54 by 33 by 22 centimetres (21.3 in × 13.0 in × 8.7 in).

title: Weston meteorite
fact: The Weston meteorite is an H4 ordinary chondrite meteorite which fell to earth above the town of Weston, Connecticut on the morning of December 14, 1807.

title: Winona meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 1928. The Winona meteorite is a primitive achondrite meteorite. It is the type specimen and by far the largest meteorite of the winonaite group.

title: Zabrodje meteorite
fact: Zabrodje is an ordinary chondrite that fell through a roof of a house in the village of Zabroddzie, Stowbtsy District approximately two hours before dawn on 22 September 1893. Only one fragment was recovered.

title: Avak crater
fact: Impact crater, 8 km across. Avak is an impact crater centered approximately 12 km (7.5 mi) southeast of Utqiagvik, Alaska, United States. Avak is a subcircular structure about 12 km (7.5 mi) in diameter and 1 km (0.62 mi) deep.

title: Azuara impact structure
fact: The Azuara structure is a structural feature of about 30 kilometres (19 mi) diameter, located in northeastern Spain, roughly 50 kilometres (31 mi) south of Zaragoza. The name is attributed to the small town of Azuara located near the center of the structure.

title: Couture crater
fact: Couture Crater is a crater in Northern Quebec, Canada. It was filled with water, making it also a lake. It is located near Hudson Bay in the Kativik territory. The crater is around 150 meters deep. Most of the lake covers an 8 km in diameter impact crater.

title: Crooked Creek crater
fact: Crooked Creek is an impact crater in Crawford County, Missouri, United States. It is 4.3 miles (7 km) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 320 ± 80 million years (Mississippian). The crater is exposed to the surface.

title: Darwin Crater
fact: Darwin Crater is a suspected meteorite impact crater in Western Tasmania about 26 km (16 mi) south of Queenstown, just within the Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park.

title: Deep Bay crater
fact: Deep Bay is a bay near the south-western tip of Reindeer Lake in Saskatchewan, Canada. The bay is strikingly circular and very deep (220 m) in an otherwise irregular and shallow lake. It is the deepest body of water in Saskatchewan.

title: Foelsche crater
fact: Foelsche is a partly buried impact structure (or astrobleme), the eroded remnant of a former impact crater. It is situated about 85 km southeast of Borroloola in the Northern Territory, Australia, and named after the nearby Foelsche River.

title: Hickman crater
fact: The Hickman crater is a recently discovered meteorite impact crater, 16 kilometres northeast of the Hope Downs 4 Mine and 35 kilometres north of Newman in the Ophthalmia Range, Western Australia.

title: Jabel Waqf as Suwwan crater
fact: The Jabal Waqf es Suwwan crater is an impact crater in Ma'an Governorate, Jordan, near the Saudi border. The crater has a diameter of 5.5 kilometres (3.4 mi). It is estimated at 37–56 million years old. It is exposed at the surface.
story_label: Wikipedia: Jabel Waqf as Suwwan crater

title: Kentland crater
fact: The Kentland structure, also known as the Kentland crater or the Kentland disturbed area, is an impact structure located near the town of Kentland in Newton County, Indiana, United States. It was discovered about 1880 when two farmers began to quarry crushed rock there.

title: Kgagodi crater
fact: Impact crater, 3.5 km across. Kgagodi is an exposed meteorite impact crater in Botswana. It is located south of the village of Kgagodi in Central Botswana.

title: Marquez crater
fact: Marquez crater is a meteorite crater located in Leon County, Texas near the small town of Marquez about 177 km (110 mi) northeast of Austin, Texas, United States. It is 12.7 km (8 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 58 ± 2 million years (Paleocene).

title: Mishina Gora crater
fact: Mishina Gora is an impact crater in European Russia, 180 kilometres southwest of St. Petersburg. It is located in Pskov Oblast of the Northwestern Federal District.

title: Mizarai crater
fact: Mizarai is a meteorite impact crater in Druskininkai municipality, Lithuania. The crater, being the second largest in the country, is not exposed to the surface and the site now hosts Mizarai village.

title: Mount Toondina crater
fact: Mount Toondina crater is an impact structure (or astrobleme), the eroded remnant of a former impact crater, located in northern South Australia in the locality of Allandale Station about 24 km (15 mi) south of the town of Oodnadatta.

title: Río Cuarto craters
fact: The Río Cuarto craters is the name given to a set of ten elongate, rimmed depressions that lie within the Pampas of Córdoba Province, (central Argentina). These depressions are aligned and distributed along a northeast to southwest trending line for a distance of 50 km (31 mi).

title: Ritland crater
fact: The Ritland crater is an impact crater at Ritland farm in Hjelmeland Municipality in eastern Rogaland county, Norway. The crater is about 15 kilometres (9.3 mi) east of the village of Hjelmelandsvågen and about 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) south of the Jøsenfjorden.

title: Wetumpka crater
fact: The Wetumpka impact crater is the only confirmed impact crater in Alabama, United States. It is located east of downtown Wetumpka in Elmore County.

title: Adzhi-Bogdo
fact: Meteorite recorded 1949. The Adzhi-Bogdo is a chondrite meteorite weighing 910 grams (32 oz). It was found on October 30, 1949, in Govi-Altay, Mongolia.

title: Angers (meteorite)
fact: Angers is an ordinary chondrite meteorite that fell in Pays de la Loire, France, at 8:15 PM on 3 June 1822.

title: Angra dos Reis meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 1.5 kg. The Angra dos Reis meteorite is the type specimen of the angrite group. It was observed when it fell to Earth in 1869.

title: Anlong (meteorite)
fact: Anlong is an H chondrite meteorite that fell to earth on May 2, 1971, in Guizhou, China.

title: Appley Bridge meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 15 kg. The Appley Bridge meteorite is a meteorite that hit ground at Halliwell Farm in Appley Bridge, Lancashire, England at around 8:45 p.m. on Tuesday, 13 October 1914.

title: Brachina meteorite
fact: Meteorite recorded 26 May 1974. The Brachina meteorite is the type specimen of the brachinites class of the asteroidal achondrites.

title: Buzzard Coulee meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 41 kg. Buzzard Coulee is the collective name of the meteorites fallen on November 20, 2008, over Saskatchewan, Canada.

title: Esquel (meteorite)
fact: Meteorite recorded 1951. Esquel is a meteorite found near Esquel, a Patagonian town in the northwest part of the province of Chubut in Argentina. It is a pallasite, a type of stony–iron meteorite that when cut and polished shows yellowish olivine (peridot) crystals.

title: Kainsaz meteorite
fact: Fifteen pieces of the Kainsaz meteorite were seen to fall near Kainsaz, Muslyumovo, Tatarstan in the Russian SFSR on September 13, 1937. The largest weighed 102.5 kilograms (226 lb), the total weight was ~200 kilograms (440 lb).

title: Mineo (meteorite)
fact: Mineo was one of the only four witnessed fall pallasite meteorites in the world, and the only one from Italy.

title: Richardton meteorite
fact: The Richardton meteorite is a 90 kilograms (200 lb) H5 Ordinary chondrite that was seen to fall at 21:48 on 30 June 1918 between Mott, North Dakota and Richardton, North Dakota, United States.

title: Winchcombe meteorite
fact: Meteorite, 602 g. The Winchcombe meteorite is a carbonaceous chondrite meteorite that was observed entering the Earth's atmosphere as a fluorescent green fireball over Gloucestershire, England, at 21:54 on 28 February 2021.

title: Wold Cottage meteorite
fact: The Wold Cottage meteorite fell near Wold Cottage farm in 1795, a few miles away from the village of Wold Newton in Yorkshire, England.

title: Calvin crater
fact: Calvin is an impact crater located in Calvin Township, Cass County, in the U.S. state of Michigan. It was discovered in 1987 by Randall Milstein of the Michigan Geological Survey while examining data from about 100 test wells drilled in the area.

title: Cerro do Jarau crater
fact: Cerro do Jarau crater is a 13.5 kilometres (8.4 mi) diameter circular feature in the Paraná Basin, Rio Grande do Sul in southern Brazil, close to the border with Uruguay. The Russian Academy of Sciences lists the structure as a probable impact crater.

title: Colônia crater
fact: The Colônia crater is a recently confirmed impact crater located in the municipality of São Paulo, Brazil.

title: Connolly Basin crater
fact: Connolly Basin is a 9 km-diameter impact crater located in the Gibson Desert of central Western Australia. It lies adjacent to the Talawana Track 45 km west of the junction (Windy Corner) with the Gary Highway, but is difficult to access due to the remoteness of the area.

title: Kalkkop crater
fact: Kalkkop is an impact crater which can be found on a private farm 50 kilometres (31 mi) south east of the town of Aberdeen, Eastern Cape, in the Eastern Cape Province of South Africa.

title: La Moinerie crater
fact: La Moinerie is an impact crater in Quebec, Canada. It is 8 km in diameter and the age is estimated to be 400 ± 50 million years (Silurian or Devonian). The crater is exposed to the surface and filled with water, forming Lac La Moinerie.

title: Luna crater
fact: The Luna crater or Luna structure is an impact crater at Luna village in Bhuj taluka of Kutch district of Gujarat, India.

title: Serpent Mound crater
fact: Serpent Mound crater, also known as the Serpent Mound Disturbance, is an eroded meteorite impact crater in Ohio, United States. It lies largely in Adams County, with the northern part mostly in Highland County, except for a small northeast part in Pike County.

title: Vargeão Dome
fact: Vargeão Dome is an impact crater in Santa Catarina, Brazil, straddling the municipalities of Vargeão, Faxinal dos Guedes, and Passos Maia.

title: Viewfield crater
fact: Viewfield is an impact crater in Saskatchewan, Canada. It is 2.5 kilometres (1.6 mi) in diameter and the age is estimated to be 190 ± 20 million years (Early Jurassic or Late Triassic). The crater is not exposed at the surface.

title: Whitecourt crater
fact: Impact crater, 36 m across. Whitecourt crater is a meteorite impact crater in central Alberta, Canada, located approximately 10 km (6.2 mi) southeast of the Town of Whitecourt within Woodlands County.

title: Yilan crater
fact: Impact crater, 1.9 km across. Yilan crater is an impact crater in China, situated to the northwest of the town of Yilan in Heilongjiang province. Its southern rim has eroded, but its northern rim is visible on the surface as a crescent-shaped ridge.

title: Ross Island, South Andaman district
fact: Ross Island, officially named Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island, is an island of the Andaman Islands. It belongs to the South Andaman administrative district, Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The island is situated 3 km (2 mi) east from central Port Blair.
story_label: Wikipedia: Ross Island, South Andaman district

title: Ryugyong Hotel
fact: The Ryugyong Hotel, sometimes spelled as Yu-Kyung Hotel, is a 330 m (1,080 ft) tall unfinished pyramid-shaped skyscraper in Pyongyang, North Korea. Its name is also one of the historical names for Pyongyang.

title: Saint Elmo, Colorado
fact: Saint Elmo is a ghost town in Chaffee County, Colorado, United States. Founded in 1880, Saint Elmo lies in the heart of the Sawatch Range, 20 miles (32 km) southwest of Buena Vista and sits at an elevation of 9,961 feet (3,036 m).

title: Saint Helena
fact: Saint Helena is a volcanic tropical island located in the South Atlantic Ocean, west of Africa. The nearest countries geographically are Angola and Namibia.

title: Salas y Gómez Island
fact: Isla Salas y Gómez, also known as Isla Sala y Gómez, is a small uninhabited Chilean island in the Pacific Ocean. It is sometimes considered the easternmost point in the Polynesian Triangle.

title: Salton Sea
fact: The Salton Sea is a shallow, landlocked, highly saline endorheic lake in Riverside and Imperial counties in Southern California. It lies on the San Andreas Fault within the Salton Trough, which stretches to the Gulf of California in Mexico.

title: Santa Claus, Indiana
fact: Santa Claus is a town in Spencer County, Indiana, United States, in the southwestern part of the state. The population was 2,586 at the 2020 census. It is home to numerous Christmas themed attractions, including Holiday World & Splashin' Safari and Santa's Candy Castle.

title: Santa Cruz Island (Galápagos)
fact: Santa Cruz Island, also known as Indefatigable Island and by other names, is the most populous and second-largest island in the Galápagos Islands, Ecuador.

title: Sanzhi UFO houses
fact: The Sanzhi UFO Houses, also known as the UFO houses of Sanjhih, Sanjhih pod houses or Sanjhih Pod City, were a set of abandoned and never-completed pod-shaped buildings in Sanzhi District, New Taipei, Taiwan.

title: Shemya
fact: Shemya or Simiya is a small island in the Semichi Islands group of the Near Islands chain in the Aleutian Islands archipelago southwest of Alaska, at 52°43′27″N 174°07′08″E. It has a land area of 5.903 sq mi (15.29 km2)…

title: Siorapaluk
fact: Siorapaluk or Hiurapaluk (Polar Inuit) is a settlement in the Qaanaaq area of the Avannaata municipality in northern Greenland. The settlement is located in the northern shore of the Siorapaluup Kangerlua (Robertson Fjord).

title: Slab City, California
fact: Slab City, also called The Slabs, is an unincorporated, off-the-grid alternative lifestyle community consisting largely of snowbirds in the Salton Trough area of the Sonoran Desert, in Imperial County, California.

title: Snowflake, Arizona
fact: Snowflake is a town in Navajo County, Arizona, United States. It was founded in 1878 by Erastus Snow and William Jordan Flake, Mormon pioneers. As of the 2020 census, Snowflake had a population of 6,104. Snowflake is 25 miles (40 km) south of Interstate 40 via Highway 77.

title: Socorro Island
fact: Socorro Island is a volcanic island in the Revillagigedo Islands, a Mexican possession lying 600 kilometres (370 mi) off the country's western coast. The size is 16.5 by 11.5 km (10.3 by 7.1 mi), with an area of 132 km2 (51 sq mi).

title: South Plaza Island
fact: South Plaza is a small island off the east coast of Santa Cruz in the Galápagos Islands. Described as having a crescent-shaped structure, the island has cliffs on the south side and low-lying shores on the north side.

title: Spreepark
fact: Spreepark is a former amusement park in the north of the Plänterwald in the Berlin district Treptow-Köpenick. It was also known by its earlier name Kulturpark Plänterwald Berlin.

title: St Kilda, Scotland
fact: St Kilda is a remote archipelago situated 35 nautical miles (65 kilometres) west-northwest of North Uist in the North Atlantic Ocean. It contains the westernmost islands of the Outer Hebrides of Scotland.

title: Stanley, Falkland Islands
fact: Stanley is the capital city of the Falkland Islands. It is located on the island of East Falkland, on a north-facing slope in one of the wettest parts of the islands.

title: Supai, Arizona
fact: Supai (Havasupai: Havasuuw) is a census-designated place (CDP) in Coconino County, Arizona, United States, within the Grand Canyon on the valley floor. As of the 2010 census, the CDP had a population of 208.

title: Taumatawhakatangi­hangakoauauotamatea­turipukakapikimaunga­horonukupokaiwhen­uakitanatahu
fact: Taumata­whakatangihanga­koauau­o­tamatea­turi­pukaka­piki­maunga­horo­nuku­pokai­whenua­ki­tana­tahu is a hill near Pōrangahau, south of Waipukurau, in southern Hawke's Bay, New Zealand. The summit of the hill is 305 metres (1,001 ft) above sea level.

title: Thurmond, West Virginia
fact: Thurmond is a town in Fayette County, West Virginia, United States, on the New River. The population was recorded as 5 in the 2020 census.

title: Tiksi
fact: Tiksi is an urban locality (an urban-type settlement) and the administrative center of Bulunsky District in the Sakha Republic, Russia, located on the shore of the Buor-Khaya Gulf of the Laptev Sea, southeast of the delta of the Lena River.

title: Times Beach, Missouri
fact: Times Beach is a ghost town in St. Louis County, Missouri, United States, 17 miles (27 km) southwest of St. Louis and 2 miles (3 km) east of Eureka.

title: Toad Suck, Arkansas
fact: Toad Suck is an unincorporated community in Perry County, Arkansas, United States. It is the location of (or is the nearest community to) Bigelow Rosenwald School, which is located at the junction of Arkansas Highway 60 and Bethel AME Road and is listed on the National Register…

title: Truth or Consequences, New Mexico
fact: Truth or Consequences (commonly T or C; founded as Hot Springs) is a city in the U.S. state of New Mexico, and the county seat of Sierra County. In 2020, the population was 6,052. The city is historically defined and economically shaped by local geothermal hot springs.
story_label: Wikipedia: Truth or Consequences, New Mexico

title: Tuktoyaktuk
fact: Tuktoyaktuk is an Inuvialuit hamlet near the Mackenzie River delta in the Inuvik Region of the Northwest Territories, Canada, at the northern terminus of the Inuvik–Tuktoyaktuk Highway.

title: Tyneham
fact: Tyneham is a ghost village abandoned in 1943 and former civil parish, now in the parish of Steeple with Tyneham, in the Dorset district, in the south of Dorset, England, near Lulworth on the Isle of Purbeck. In 2001 the civil parish had a population of 0.

title: Ushuaia
fact: Ushuaia is the capital of Tierra del Fuego, Antártida e Islas del Atlántico Sur Province, Argentina. With a population of 89,606 and a location below the 54th parallel south latitude, Ushuaia claims the title of world's southernmost city.

title: Utqiagvik, Alaska
fact: Utqiaġvik, formerly known as Barrow, is the borough seat and largest city of the North Slope Borough in the U.S. state of Alaska.

title: Varosha, Famagusta
fact: Varosha is the southern quarter of Famagusta, a de jure territory of Cyprus, currently under the control of Northern Cyprus. Varosha had a population of 226 in the 2011 Northern Cyprus census. The area of Varosha is 6.19 km2 (2.39 sq mi).

title: Verkhoyansk
fact: Verkhoyansk is a town in Verkhoyansky District of the Sakha Republic, Russia, located on the Yana River in the Arctic Circle, 92 kilometers (57 mi) from Batagay, the administrative center of the district, and 675 kilometers (419 mi) north of Yakutsk…

title: Vilarinho da Furna
fact: Vilarinho da Furna (alternately called Vilarinho das Furnas) was a former village, located in the civil parish of Campo de Gerês, in the municipality of Terras de Bouro, in the northern Portuguese district of Braga.

title: Villa Epecuén
fact: Villa Epecuén is an abandoned tourist village in Buenos Aires Province, Argentina, on the eastern shore of Laguna Epecuén, about 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) north of the city of Carhué.

title: Villa O'Higgins
fact: Villa O'Higgins is a small town in the Aysén Region of southern Chile, located 220 km south of Cochrane and 550 km south of Coyhaique.

title: Villa Puerto Edén
fact: Villa Puerto Edén is a Chilean hamlet and minor port located in Wellington Island, in Natales commune, Última Esperanza Province, Magallanes Region. It is considered one of Chile's most isolated inhabited places together with Easter Island and Villa Las Estrellas.

title: Why, Arizona
fact: Why is an unincorporated rural community in Pima County, Arizona, United States. It lies near the western border of the Tohono Oʼodham Indian Reservation and due north of Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument in Southern Arizona.

title: Wittenoom, Western Australia
fact: Wittenoom is a former mining town and a declared contaminated site, 1,420 kilometres (880 mi) north-north-east of Perth, in the Hamersley Range in the Pilbara region of Western Australia.

title: Y (commune)
fact: Y is a commune in the Somme department in Hauts-de-France in northern France. Y bears the shortest place name in France, and one of the shortest in the world.

title: Zzyzx, California
fact: Zzyzx ( ZY-ziks), formerly Soda Springs, is an unincorporated area in San Bernardino County, California, United States, within the boundaries of the Mojave National Preserve, managed by the National Park Service (NPS), an agency of the U.S. Department of Interior, as public land.

title: La Güera
fact: La Güera is a ghost town on the Atlantic coast at the southern tip of Western Sahara, on the western side of the Ras Nouadhibou peninsula which is split in two by the Mauritania–Western Sahara border, 15 kilometres (9.3 mi) west of Nouadhibou.

title: Oatman, Arizona
fact: Oatman is a census-designated place (CDP) in the Black Mountains of Mohave County, Arizona, United States, at an elevation of 2,710 feet (830 m).

title: Yukhari Askipara
fact: Yukhari Askipara, also known as Verin Voskepar, is an abandoned village in an exclave of the Gazakh District of Azerbaijan.

title: Chinese Camp, California
fact: Chinese Camp is a census-designated place (CDP) in Tuolumne County, California, United States. The population was 90 at the 2020 census, down from 126 at the 2010 census, which was down from 146 at the 2000 census.

title: Darwin, California
fact: Darwin is an unincorporated former mining community in Inyo County, California, United States. It is located 22 miles (35 km) southeast of Keeler. For statistical purposes, the United States Census Bureau has defined Darwin as a census-designated place (CDP).

title: Bayport, Florida
fact: Bayport is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Hernando County, Florida, United States. As of the 2020 census, Bayport had a population of 45.

title: Elkport, Iowa
fact: Elkport is a city in Clayton County, Iowa, United States. The population was 29 at the time of the 2020 census, down from 88 in 2000.

title: Tuleta, Texas
fact: Tuleta is a census-designated place (CDP) in Bee County, Texas, United States. The population was 231 at the 2020 census.

title: Keeler, California
fact: Keeler, formerly known as Hawley, is an unincorporated community in Inyo County, California, United States. Keeler is located on the east shore of Owens Lake 11.5 miles (19 km) south-southeast of New York Butte.

title: Laupāhoehoe, Hawaii
fact: Laupāhoehoe is a census-designated place (CDP) in Hawaiʻi County, Hawaii, United States, in the District of North Hilo. The population was 581 at the 2010 census, up from 473 at the 2000 census.

title: Tehuacana, Texas
fact: Tehuacana is a town near the Tehuacana Hills in Limestone County, Texas, United States. The population was 228 at the 2020 census. From 1869 until 1902, the town was home to Trinity University.

title: Cayuga, Oklahoma
