fact: Stratovolcano, 1,580 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2015. The Lokong-Empung volcanic complex, rising above the plain of Tondano in North Sulawesi, includes four peaks and an active crater. Lokon, the highest peak, has a flat craterless top.

title: Funka Asane
fact: Stratovolcano, -20 m in Japan. Last erupted 2022. Eruptions have been recorded since the 18th century from Funka Asane, a submarine edifice ~4 km NW of Kita-Ioto, the northernmost of the Kazan Retto (Volcano Islands), in the southern Ogasawara Volcanic Arc.

title: Toya
fact: Stratovolcano, 733 m in Japan. Last erupted 2001. Usuzan, one of Hokkaido's most well-known volcanoes, is a small stratovolcano located astride the southern topographic rim of the 110,000-year-old Toya caldera.

title: Karymsky
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,513 m in Russia. Last erupted 2025. Karymsky is a symmetrical stratovolcano constructed within a 5-km-wide caldera that formed during the early Holocene.

title: St. Paul
fact: Stratovolcano, 268 m in France. Last erupted 1793. The uninhabited triangular island of St. Paul is located near the axis of the East Indian Ocean Ridge, 80 km S of Amsterdam Island.

title: Fukutoku-Oka-no-Ba
fact: Pyroclastic cone, -29 m in Japan. Last erupted 2021. Fukutoku-Oka-no-ba is a submarine volcano located 5 km NE of the island of Minami-Ioto. Water discoloration is frequently observed, and several ephemeral islands have formed in the 20th century.

title: Tangkuban Parahu
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,084 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2019. Gunung Tangkuban Parahu is a broad stratovolcano overlooking Indonesia's former capital city of Bandung. The volcano was constructed within the 6 x 8 km Pleistocene Sunda caldera, which formed about 190,000 years ago.

title: Adatarayama
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,728 m in Japan. Last erupted 1996. The broad forested massif of Adatarayama volcano is located E of Bandai volcano, about 15 km SW of Fukushima city.

title: Farallon de Pajaros
fact: Stratovolcano, 337 m in United States. Last erupted 1953. The small 2-km-wide island of Farallon de Pajaros is the northernmost and most active volcano of the Mariana Islands.

title: Tokachidake
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,077 m in Japan. Last erupted 2004. Tokachidake volcano consists of a group of dominantly andesitic stratovolcanoes and lava domes arranged on a NE-SW line above a plateau of welded Pleistocene tuffs in central Hokkaido.

title: Ketoi
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,172 m in Russia. Last erupted 1960. The circular 10-km-wide Ketoi island, which rises across the 19-km-wide Diana Strait from Simushir Island, hosts of one of the most complex volcanic structures of the Kuril Islands.

title: Raikoke
fact: Stratovolcano, 551 m in Russia. Last erupted 2019. A low truncated volcano forms the small barren Raikoke Island, which lies 16 km across the Golovnin Strait from Matua Island in the central Kuriles.

title: Kharimkotan
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,145 m in Russia. Last erupted 1933. The 8 x 12 km island of Kharimkotan in the northern Kuriles consists of a stratovolcano cut by two breached depressions on the east and NW sides.

title: Rincon de la Vieja
fact: Complex volcano, 1,729 m in Costa Rica. Last erupted 2024. Rincón de la Vieja is a volcanic complex in the Guanacaste Range of NW Costa Rica. Sometimes referred to as the Rincon de la Vieja-Santa María Volcanic Complex…
story_label: Wikipedia: Rincón de la Vieja Volcano

title: Marchena
fact: Shield volcano, 343 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 1991. The low shield volcano forming Marchena Island contains one of the largest calderas of the Galápagos Islands.

title: Kverkfjoll
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,930 m in Iceland. Last erupted 1968. Kverkfjöll is a large subglacial volcano at the NE end of the Vatnajökull icecap. Two elliptical ice-filled calderas, each about 8 x 5 km in size, have been identified.

title: Nightingale Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 365 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 2004. Nightingale Island, along with the adjacent smaller Middle (or Alex) and Stoltenhoff Islands and associated small islets, are the southernmost of the Tristan da Cunha island group.

title: Gede-Pangrango
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,026 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1957. The two peaks of the Gede-Pangrango volcanic complex overlook the major cities of Cianjur, Sukabumi, and Bogor, situated to the E, S, and NW, respectively.

title: Soputan
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,785 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2020. The Soputan stratovolcano on the southern rim of the Quaternary Tondano caldera on the northern arm of Sulawesi Island is one of Sulawesi's most active volcanoes.

title: Karangetang
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,797 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2023. Karangetang (Api Siau) volcano lies at the northern end of the island of Siau, about 125 km NNE of the NE-most point of Sulawesi. The stratovolcano contains five summit craters along a N-S line.

title: Myojinsho
fact: Caldera, 11 m in Japan. Last erupted 1970. Beyonesu Rocks are part of the barely exposed rim of the largely submarine Myojinsho caldera.

title: Izu-Torishima
fact: Stratovolcano, 394 m in Japan. Last erupted 2002. The circular, 2.7-km-wide island of Izu-Torishima in the southern Izu Islands is capped by an unvegetated summit cone formed during an eruption in 1939.

title: Pavlof
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,493 m in United States. Last erupted 2022. The most active volcano of the Aleutian arc, Pavlof is a Holocene stratovolcano that was constructed along a line of vents extending NE from the Emmons Lake caldera.

title: Wrangell
fact: Shield volcano, 4,278 m in United States. Last erupted 1912. Mount Wrangell is one of the world's largest continental-margin volcanoes, with a diameter of 30 km at 2,000 m elevation.

title: Irruputuncu
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,163 m in Chile-Bolivia. Last erupted 1995. Irruputuncu is a small stratovolcano that straddles the Chile/Bolivia border. It is the youngest and most southerly of a NE-SW-trending chain of volcanoes.

title: Azul, Cerro
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,788 m in Chile. Last erupted 1967. The Cerro Azul stratovolcano is at the southern end of the Descabezado Grande-Cerro Azul eruptive system. It is a steep-sided edifice with a 500-m-wide summit crater open to the north.

title: Tristan da Cunha
fact: Shield volcano, 2,060 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 1962. Tristan da Cunha is a 13-km-wide island volcano lying about 500 km E of the crest of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge just south of the latitudes of Buenos Aires and Cape Town.

title: Tair, Jebel at
fact: Stratovolcano, 244 m in Yemen. Last erupted 2008. The basaltic Jebel at Tair volcano rises from 1,200 m depth in the south-central Red Sea, forming an oval-shaped island about 3 km long.

title: Arjuno-Welirang
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,343 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1952. The Arjuno and Welirang volcanoes anchor the SE and NW ends, respectively, of a 6-km-long line of volcanic cones and craters.

title: Kuchinoerabujima
fact: Stratovolcano, 657 m in Japan. Last erupted 2020. A group of young stratovolcanoes forms the eastern end of the irregularly shaped island of Kuchinoerabujima in the northern Ryukyu Islands, 15 km W of Yakushima.

title: Iwatesan
fact: Complex volcano, 2,038 m in Japan. Last erupted 1919. Viewed from the east, Iwatesan volcano has a symmetrical profile that invites comparison with Fuji, but on the west an older cone is visible containing an oval-shaped, 1.8 x 3 km caldera.

title: Shikotsu
fact: Caldera, 1,320 m in Japan. Last erupted 1981. The 13 x 15 km Shikotsu caldera, largely filled by the waters of Lake Shikotsu, was formed during one of Hokkaido's largest Quaternary eruptions about 31-34,000 years ago.

title: Rasshua
fact: Stratovolcano, 956 m in Russia. Last erupted 1957. The elongated 6 x 13 km island of Rasshua in the central Kuriles contains three overlapping central cones within a 6 km caldera whose eastern margin is beyond the shoreline.

title: Ebeko
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,103 m in Russia. Last erupted 2024. The flat-topped summit of the central cone of Ebeko volcano, one of the most active in the Kuril Islands, occupies the northern end of Paramushir Island.

title: Telica
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,036 m in Nicaragua. Last erupted 2025. Telica, one of Nicaragua's most active volcanoes, has erupted frequently since the beginning of the Spanish era. This volcano group consists of several interlocking cones and vents with a general NW alignment.

title: Cumbal
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,764 m in Colombia. Last erupted 1926. Many youthful lava flows extend from the glacier-capped Cumbal volcano, the southernmost historically active volcano of Colombia.

title: Montagu Island
fact: Shield volcano, 1,370 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 2007. The largest of the South Sandwich Islands, Montagu consists of a massive shield volcano cut by a 6-km-wide ice-filled summit caldera.

title: Talang
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,575 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2007. Talang is part of a large volcanic edifice just NW of Dibawah Lake. An older volcanic peak, Pasar Arbaao, is ~1.5 km W. The steep-sided Talang cone exhibits fumarolic activity but has no crater…

title: Mutnovsky
fact: Complex volcano, 2,288 m in Russia. Last erupted 2000. Massive Mutnovsky, one of the most active volcanoes of southern Kamchatka, is formed of four coalescing stratovolcanoes of predominantly basaltic composition. Multiple summit craters cap the volcanic complex.

title: Kizimen
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,334 m in Russia. Last erupted 2013. Kizimen is an isolated, conical stratovolcano that is morphologically similar to St. Helens prior to its 1980 eruption.

title: Alcedo
fact: Shield volcano, 1,130 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 1993. Alcedo is one of the lowest and smallest of six shield volcanoes on Isabela Island. Much of the flanks and summit caldera are vegetated, but young lava flows are prominent on the N flank near the saddle with Darwin volcano.

title: Tupungatito
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,660 m in Chile-Argentina. Last erupted 1987. Tupungatito volcano, the northernmost historically active volcano of the central Chilean Andes, is located along the Chile-Argentina border about 90 km E of Santiago and immediately SW of the Pleistocene Tupungato…

title: Southern Thule
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,075 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 1975. The Southern Thule island group, at the southern end of the South Sandwich island arc bordering the Scotia Sea, consist of three stratovolcanoes constructed along an E-W line.

title: Halla
fact: Shield volcano, 1,919 m in South Korea. Last erupted 1007. The massive Halla shield volcano forms much of the 40 x 80 km Cheju (Jeju) Island, which lies 90 km S of the Korean Peninsula.

title: Ascension
fact: Stratovolcano, 822 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 1508. Ascensión Island, just west of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge ~2,250 km E of the eastern-most point of Brazil, is the 12-km-diameter emergent summit of a stratovolcano that rises ~3,000 m above the seafloor.

title: Ciremai
fact: Stratovolcano, 3,039 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 1951. The symmetrical Ciremai stratovolcano is located closer to the northern coast than other central Java volcanoes.

title: Paluweh
fact: Stratovolcano, 875 m in Indonesia. Last erupted 2013. Paluweh, also known as Rokatenda, forms the 8-km-wide island of Palu'e north of the volcanic arc that cuts across Flores Island.

title: Camiguin
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,552 m in Philippines. Last erupted 1953. The 20-km-long Camiguin Island just off the coast of north-central Mindanao Island consists of four overlapping stratovolcanoes overlying older buried edifices.

title: Kusatsu-Shiranesan
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,165 m in Japan. Last erupted 2018. The Kusatsu-Shiranesan complex, located immediately north of Asama volcano, consists of a series of overlapping pyroclastic cones and three crater lakes.

title: Chokaisan
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,236 m in Japan. Last erupted 1974. Chokaisan is composed of two overlapping stratovolcanoes with a conical profile that inspired the local names of Akita-Fuji or Dewa-Fuji.

title: Kanaga
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,307 m in United States. Last erupted 2023. Symmetrical Kanaga stratovolcano is situated within the Kanaton caldera at the northern tip of Kanaga Island.

title: Bogoslof
fact: Stratovolcano, 150 m in United States. Last erupted 2017. Bogoslof is the emergent summit of a submarine volcano that lies 40 km N of the main Aleutian arc. It rises 1,500 m above the Bering Sea floor.

title: Akutan
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,303 m in United States. Last erupted 1992. Akutan contains a 2-km-wide caldera with a large cinder cone in the NE part of the caldera that has been the source of frequent explosive eruptions and occasional lava effusion that covers the caldera floor.

title: Miravalles
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,028 m in Costa Rica. Last erupted 1946. Miravalles is an andesitic stratovolcano that is one of five post-caldera cones along a NE-trending line within the broad 15 x 20 km Guayabo (Miravalles) caldera.

title: Isluga
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,550 m in Chile. Last erupted 1913. The broad Isluga volcano lies 7 km W of the Chile/Bolivia border at the W end of a group of volcanoes extending to Tata Sabaya volcano in Bolivia.

title: Bristol Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,100 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 2016. The 9 x 10 km Bristol Island near the southern end of the South Sandwich arc lies across Fortser's Passage from the Southern Thule Islands and forms one of the largest islands of the chain.

title: Candlemas Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 550 m in United Kingdom. Last erupted 1911. The southern end of Candlemas Island consists of an eroded, glacier-covered basaltic stratovolcano cut by steep cliffs on the east.

title: Oraefajokull
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,010 m in Iceland. Last erupted 1728. Öræfajökull, Iceland's highest peak, is a broad glacier-clad central volcano at the SE end of the Vatnajökull icecap. A 4 x 5 km subglacial caldera truncates the summit of the dominantly basaltic and rhyolitic volcano.

title: Fagradalsfjall
fact: Fissure vent, 250 m in Iceland. Last erupted 2023. Although the Fagradalsfjall fissure swarm has previously been considered a split or secondary swarm of the Krýsuvík–Trölladyngja volcanic system…

title: Eldey
fact: Fissure vent, 70 m in Iceland. Last erupted 1926. The Eldey volcanic system is located on the northernmost part of the Reykjanes Ridge and is submarine with the exception of Eldey Island and the skerries (small rocky islands) Eldeyjardrangur, Geirfugladrangur, and Geirfuglasker.

title: Raoul Island
fact: Stratovolcano, 516 m in New Zealand. Last erupted 2006. Anvil-shaped Raoul Island is the largest and northernmost of the Kermadec Islands. During the past several thousand years volcanism has been dominated by dacitic explosive eruptions.

title: Karkar
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,839 m in Papua New Guinea. Last erupted 1979. Karkar is a 19 x 25 km forest-covered island that is truncated by two nested summit calderas. The 5.5 km outer caldera was formed during one or more eruptions, the last of which occurred 9,000 years ago.

title: Izu-Tobu
fact: Pyroclastic cone, 580 m in Japan. Last erupted 1989. The Izu-Tobu (or Higashi-Izu) volcano group is scattered over a broad, plateau-like area of more than 400 km2 on the E side of the Izu Peninsula.

title: Zaozan [Zaosan]
fact: Complex volcano, 1,841 m in Japan. Last erupted 1940. The Zaozan (or Zaosan) volcano group consists of a complex cluster of stratovolcanoes in north-central Honshu about 40 km W of Sendai Bay.

title: Semisopochnoi
fact: Stratovolcano, 1,221 m in United States. Last erupted 2023. Semisopochnoi, the largest subaerial volcano of the western Aleutians, is 20 km wide at sea level and contains an 8-km-wide caldera.

title: Azul, Cerro
fact: Shield volcano, 1,640 m in Ecuador. Last erupted 2008. Located at the SW tip of the J-shaped Isabela Island, Cerro Azul contains a steep-walled 4 x 5 km nested summit caldera complex that is one of the smallest diameter, but at 650 m one of the deepest in the Galápagos Islands.

title: Tinguiririca
fact: Stratovolcano, 4,280 m in Chile. Last erupted 1917. Tinguiririca is composed of at least seven Holocene scoria cones W of the Chile-Argentina border constructed along a NNE-SSW fissure over an eroded Pleistocene stratovolcano.

title: Kazbek
fact: Stratovolcano, 5,004 m in Georgia. Last erupted 750 BCE. The glacier-covered Kazbek stratovolcano in the Caucasus Mountains of Georgia, just south of the border with Russia, has produced long lava flows down flank valleys.

title: Haleakala
fact: Shield volcano, 3,053 m in United States. Last erupted 1750. The massive Haleakala shield volcano forms the eastern portion of the island of Maui. The summit is at the NW end of a volcanic ridge and at the head of a large scarp that opens to the ENE…

title: Pico
fact: Stratovolcano, 2,351 m in Portugal. Last erupted 1720. The conical Pico stratovolcano occupies the western end of Pico Island and is the highest volcano in the Azores.

title: Tinakula
fact: Stratovolcano, 796 m in Solomon Islands. Last erupted 2024. The small 3.5-km-wide island of Tinakula is the exposed summit of a massive stratovolcano at the NW end of the Santa Cruz islands. It has a breached summit crater that extends from the summit to below sea level.
